A workspace is the mutable unit a client writes into. It is based on one snapshot and points at a head snapshot that moves as the client publishes checkpoints. A workspace moves through states such as CREATING, IDLE, MOUNTED, CHECKPOINTING, EXPIRING, and DELETED.

Optimistic concurrency guards each workspace. A version counter advances on every update. A writer publishes a checkpoint by comparing the version it read against the current value, then advancing it inside one transaction. If the version changed, the writer retries.

A workspace lease grants one host the right to write to a workspace. At most one lease generation is active for a workspace at a time. The lease moves through ISSUED, ACTIVE, RELEASING, RELEASED, EXPIRED, and REVOKED. This single-active-writer lease is how AWC keeps one writer per workspace.

docs.title: Mount sessions and tickets
docs.text:
A mount session is one live mount of a workspace on a host. The mode is READ_ONLY or READ_WRITE. A mount session moves through REQUESTED, AUTHORIZED, PREPARING, MOUNTED, UNMOUNTING, CLOSED, and FAILED. A read-write mount holds the active workspace lease.

A mount ticket is a signed authorization to mount a given snapshot on a given host. It carries a nonce, a target policy, and an expiry, and the control plane signs it. A ticket can be revoked before it expires.

docs.title: Job queue
docs.text:
A job is a unit of background work. Jobs carry a kind, a payload, and a result. A job moves through PENDING, RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED, and CANCELLED. Workers claim pending jobs and lock them while the jobs run. Each job retries up to a configured maximum.

A job may carry a dedupe key. At most one active job is kept for a given kind, tenant, and dedupe key. A null dedupe key is never deduped.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text: An idempotency key caches the outcome of an API call so that a retry returns the same result. The composite key is the tenant, the principal, the operation, and the client-supplied key. An idempotency row is PENDING, COMPLETED, or FAILED, and it expires after a set time.

docs.title: Garbage collection
docs.text:
Garbage collection runs in epochs of mark-and-sweep.

A GC run is one epoch for a tenant. It records the cutoff, whether the run was a dry run, and counts of roots, marked digests, store inventory, deletion candidates, and deleted objects. It also records the bytes reclaimed.

A GC deletion plan is one candidate digest in an epoch. It records the digest, its kind and size, and whether it was deleted or skipped.

A GC integrity hold pins a digest so that sweep cannot delete it while scrub or recovery is pending.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text: A retention policy sets how long the control plane keeps snapshots, checkpoints, failed imports, and exports. A policy is scoped to a tenant or to a project inside a tenant.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text: The audit log is append-only. A row records the tenant, the principal, the action, the resource type and id, a request id, and a JSON detail payload. There is no update or delete path on the audit log.

docs.title: Environment variable reference
docs.text:
AWC reads configuration from environment variables. This page lists every AWC_* variable the current build reads, the binary that reads it, the default, and the effect. Values come from the code, not from memory. Where the code and the spec disagree, the code wins and the disagreement is noted.

Two non-AWC_ variables are required peers and are listed at the end: DATABASE_URL and AWCD_SOCKET.

docs.title: Nested config convention (awcd only)
docs.text:
awcd loads a layered config (file, then environment, then flags). The environment layer reads flat fields as AWC_<FIELD> and nested fields as AWC_<SECTION>__<FIELD>. The double underscore separates a config section from a field.

Field path Environment variable host_id AWC_HOST_ID control_plane_endpoint AWC_CONTROL_PLANE_ENDPOINT cache.max_bytes AWC_CACHE__MAX_BYTES leases.expiry_seconds AWC_LEASES__EXPIRY_SECONDS

Field names map from snake_case to SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. allowed_bind_roots is a comma-separated list. Integer fields must parse as non-negative integers, or startup fails with a ParseValue error.

Only awcd reads this structured layer. awc-control and awc-worker read their own direct variables (see the tables below).

docs.title: Structured config variables (awcd)
docs.text: Read by awcd from the structured environment layer. Layer order is file, then environment, then flags; later layers override earlier ones.

docs.title: Top-level fields
docs.text:
Variable Type Default Effect AWC_HOST_ID string none, required Local host identifier, host_<ulid>. Startup fails if unset or malformed. AWC_CONTROL_PLANE_ENDPOINT URL none, required Control plane URL. Schemes http and https only. AWC_BASEFS_MOUNT absolute path none, required Internal mount point for the read-only base filesystem. AWC_CACHE_ROOT absolute path none, required Root directory of the local content cache. AWC_WORKSPACE_ROOT absolute path none, required Root directory for per-workspace merged mounts. AWC_ALLOWED_BIND_ROOTS comma-separated paths empty list Host paths that may be bind targets. Each path must be absolute. AWC_HEALTH_HTTP_LISTEN host:port unset (HTTP server disabled) Loopback address for the liveness, readiness, and metrics HTTP server.

The three roots (basefs_mount, cache_root, workspace_root) must be distinct. Startup rejects any pair that is equal.

docs.title: Cache limits
docs.text:
Default to the built-in cache defaults when unset.

Variable Type Default Effect AWC_CACHE__MAX_BYTES u64 1000000000000 (1 TiB) Total byte limit of the local cache. Must be greater than zero. AWC_CACHE__MIN_FREE_BYTES u64 50000000000 (50 GiB) Minimum free space to preserve on the host filesystem. AWC_CACHE__MAX_REMOTE_FETCHES u32 128 Bounded object-store read concurrency. AWC_CACHE__MAX_REMOTE_FETCHES_PER_TENANT u32 32 Per-tenant object-store read concurrency. Cannot exceed the global limit. AWC_CACHE__MAX_PREFETCH_FETCHES u32 8 Prefetch concurrency. Cannot exceed the global limit.

docs.title: Checkpoint limits
docs.text:
Default to the built-in checkpoint defaults when unset.

Variable Type Default Effect AWC_CHECKPOINT__MAX_CONCURRENT u32 4 Maximum concurrent checkpoint uploads. Must be greater than zero. AWC_CHECKPOINT__FREEZE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS u64 10 Freeze and quiesce timeout for cutting a checkpoint, in seconds. Must be greater than zero. AWC_CHECKPOINT__PRESERVE_LOCAL_GRACE_SECONDS u64 3600 Grace period for preserving local changes after a checkpoint, in seconds. Must be greater than zero.

docs.title: Lease timing
docs.text:
Default to the built-in lease defaults when unset.

Variable Type Default Effect AWC_LEASES__RENEW_INTERVAL_SECONDS u64 30 How often the holder renews the lease, in seconds. Must be less than expiry_seconds. AWC_LEASES__EXPIRY_SECONDS u64 90 Lease lifetime before automatic expiry, in seconds. AWC_LEASES__DISCONNECTED_GRACE_SECONDS u64 60 Grace period for a disconnected holder before revocation, in seconds. Must be greater than zero.

docs.title: Object store selection
docs.text:
AWC_CAS_URL selects the backing object store. Read by awcd, awc-control, and awc-worker.

Variable Type Default Effect AWC_CAS_URL URL string memory:// (awcd, awc-control); required, no default (awc-worker) Object store transport. memory:// is the in-process store. s3:// selects the S3-compatible transport and requires the s3 feature plus the AWC_S3_* variables. Any other scheme is a startup error.

docs.title: S3 transport variables
docs.text:
Read when AWC_CAS_URL is s3://. The s3 feature must be enabled.

Variable Type Default Effect AWC_S3_ENDPOINT URL string none, required S3-compatible endpoint URL. Must be https:// unless AWC_S3_ALLOW_HTTP=1. AWC_S3_BUCKET string none, required Bucket name. A path suffix after the bucket becomes the key prefix. AWC_S3_REGION string us-east-1 SigV4 signing region. B2 encodes it in the endpoint host (e.g. eu-central-003). AWC_S3_KEY_PREFIX string empty Key prefix applied to every object (normalized to end with /). Required when the credentials are restricted to a prefix, e.g. a B2 namePrefix-scoped key. AWC_S3_ALLOW_HTTP 0/1 0 Explicit opt-in for plaintext http:// endpoints (cluster-local MinIO in dev, CI, and the Helm chart default). Any other value is ignored. AWC_S3_CONDITIONAL_CREATE 0/1 endpoint-dependent 1 sends If-None-Match: * on puts even when the endpoint default is off; 0 disables it. Default is off for *.backblazeb2.com/*.backblazeb.com (B2 rejects the header), on otherwise. AWC_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID string none Access key id. Part of a credential pair. AWC_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY string none Secret access key. Part of a credential pair. AWC_S3_SESSION_TOKEN string none (absent) Temporary session token. Read only when both the access key id and the secret are present.

Credentials load only when both AWC_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWC_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are set. Otherwise requests are made with no credentials.

docs.title: Control plane (awc-control)
docs.text:
Read by the awc-control server.

Variable Type Default Effect AWC_CONTROL_LISTEN host:port 127.0.0.1:8080 REST API listen address. AWC_CONTROL_GRPC_LISTEN host:port 127.0.0.1:8081 Internal gRPC listen address. AWC_CONTROL_TLS_CERT file path none, required outside dev Server TLS certificate file. Read for mutual-TLS gRPC. AWC_CONTROL_TLS_KEY file path none, required outside dev Server TLS private key file. AWC_CONTROL_TLS_CLIENT_CA file path none, required outside dev Client CA certificate file. Clients must present a certificate signed by this CA. AWC_SERVICE_TOKEN_KEY string none, required outside dev Secret key for signing service-account tokens. Required unless AWC_DEV_MODE=1. AWC_MOUNT_TICKET_SEED 64-char hex none, required outside dev 32-byte seed for signing mount tickets. Decoded from hex. AWC_MOUNT_TARGET_ROOTS comma-separated paths /opt/sandboxes Target-path roots stamped into every issued mount ticket.

Outside AWC_DEV_MODE=1, the three server TLS variables, AWC_SERVICE_TOKEN_KEY, and AWC_MOUNT_TICKET_SEED are all required. Startup fails if any is unset.

docs.title: Control-plane client TLS (awcd)
docs.text:
Read by awcd when it connects to an https:// control plane.

Variable Type Default Effect AWC_CONTROL_TLS_CA file path none, required for https:// CA certificate file that signs the control plane server certificate. AWC_CONTROL_TLS_CERT file path none, required for https:// Client certificate file for mutual TLS. AWC_CONTROL_TLS_KEY file path none, required for https:// Client private key file for mutual TLS.

For an https:// endpoint, all three are required. For an http:// endpoint, the connection is refused unless AWC_DEV_MODE=1.

docs.title: Worker (awc-worker)
docs.text:
Read by the awc-worker binary.

Variable Type Default Effect AWC_WORKER_ID string awc-worker Per-process identifier. Each concurrent worker adds a -<n> suffix on its leases. AWC_WORKER_CONCURRENCY integer 4 Bounded worker count. AWC_WORKER_LEASE_SECS integer 300 Job visibility-lease length, in seconds. AWC_WORKER_POLL_INTERVAL_MS integer 1000 Idle poll interval, in milliseconds. AWC_RETENTION_GRACE_SECS integer 86400 How long an EXPIRING workspace stays reversible before it may be reaped.

docs.title: Garbage collection (awc-worker)
docs.text:
Read by awc-worker.

Variable Type Default Effect AWC_GC_GRACE_SECS integer 86400 Durable-GC safety grace. Objects newer than now - grace are never swept. AWC_GC_BATCH_SIZE integer 1000 Maximum candidate count deleted per epoch. AWC_GC_CANARY_SIZE integer 10 Size of the leading canary batch. AWC_GC_DRY_RUN 1, true, or TRUE unset (false) Plan only, delete nothing. Any other value means false.

docs.title: Host daemon (awcd)
docs.text: Variable Type Default Effect AWC_CGROUP_ROOTS colon-separated paths empty Cgroup roots scanned by the checkpoint runner.

docs.title: CLI output and connection (awcctl)
docs.text:
Read by awcctl global flags. Each variable maps to a global --flag, which overrides the environment.

Variable Type Default Effect AWC_OUTPUT enum: text or json text Output format. json is machine-readable. AWC_QUIET boolean false Suppress progress output on stderr. Results still print. AWC_HOST_SOCKET path /run/awcd/awcd.sock Path to the local awcd Unix socket. AWC_CONTROL_ENDPOINT URL none Base URL of the remote control plane. Required for control-plane commands. AWC_TOKEN string none Bearer token for control-plane authentication. AWC_TENANT string none Tenant id. Required for control-plane and snapshot-upload commands. AWC_PROJECT string none Project id. Required for most control-plane commands. AWC_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY string none Idempotency key for the next mutating request.

Socket defaults agree

AWC_HOST_SOCKET defaults to /run/awcd/awcd.sock in awcctl. The awcd binary uses the same default (set by positional argument or AWCD_SOCKET), and the systemd unit creates /run/awcd through RuntimeDirectory=awcd. When you run awcd without systemd, pass the socket path explicitly to both binaries.

docs.title: Authentication and mount tickets
docs.text:
Variable Type Default Read by Effect AWC_SERVICE_TOKEN_KEY string none, required outside dev awc-control Secret key for signing service-account tokens. AWC_MOUNT_TICKET_SEED 64-char hex none, required outside dev awc-control 32-byte signing seed for issued mount tickets. AWC_MOUNT_TICKET_PUBLIC_KEY 64-char hex none, required outside dev awcd Public half of the mount-ticket signing key. Used to verify tickets. AWC_MOUNT_TICKET_PUBLIC_KEY_FILE file path none awcd File that contains the 64-char hex public key. Used only when AWC_MOUNT_TICKET_PUBLIC_KEY is unset.

awcd reads AWC_MOUNT_TICKET_PUBLIC_KEY first, then falls back to AWC_MOUNT_TICKET_PUBLIC_KEY_FILE. Outside AWC_DEV_MODE=1, at least one must be set.

docs.title: Dev mode
docs.text:
AWC_DEV_MODE is the master dev switch. When set to 1, several production guards relax. Read by awc-control (REST and gRPC setup) and awcd.

Variable Type Default Effect AWC_DEV_MODE 1 to enable unset (production) When 1: awc-control skips the mutual-TLS gRPC setup and does not require AWC_SERVICE_TOKEN_KEY or AWC_MOUNT_TICKET_SEED; awcd allows http:// control-plane endpoints and falls back to a fixed dev ticket key.

The variables below are read only by awc-control, and only when AWC_DEV_BOOTSTRAP=1. They seed a local-dev identity. They have no effect otherwise.

Variable Type Default Effect AWC_DEV_BOOTSTRAP 1 to enable unset When 1: grant the dev principal the Admin role on the dev project and mint a full-scope service token. AWC_DEV_TENANT string ten_01arz3ndektsv4rrffq69g5fav Tenant id for the bootstrapped identity. AWC_DEV_PROJECT string prj_01arz3ndektsv4rrffq69g5fav Project id for the bootstrapped identity. AWC_DEV_PRINCIPAL string prin_01arz3ndektsv4rrffq69g5fav Principal id for the bootstrapped identity.

The dev token is minted only when AWC_SERVICE_TOKEN_KEY is also set. The bootstrap seeds a local-dev identity.

docs.title: Test-only variables
docs.text:
These gate integration tests. They are not read by production code paths.

Variable Type Default Read by Effect AWC_PG_TESTS 1 to enable unset awc-db, awc-control, awc-worker tests When 1, Postgres integration tests run. If DATABASE_URL is empty, the test binary fails with a clear message. AWC_S3_TESTS 1 to enable unset awc-cas tests When 1, S3 integration tests run and require AWC_S3_ENDPOINT and AWC_S3_BUCKET.

docs.title: Related non-AWC variables
docs.text: Variable Type Default Read by Effect DATABASE_URL string none, required awc-control, awc-worker PostgreSQL connection string. Startup fails if unset. AWCD_SOCKET path /run/awcd/awcd.sock awcd Unix socket path for the awcd host API. Overridden by the second positional argument to awcd.

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text:
• The structured AWC_<SECTION>__<FIELD> layer is read only by awcd. awc-control and awc-worker do not load it; they read their own direct variables listed above.
  • There is no environment variable for the REST rate limiter. awc-control constructs an unlimited rate limiter in code. Throttling (spec §16.10) has no env knob in this build.
  • OIDC discovery is not wired. Only service-account tokens authenticate. The verifier starts from an empty static set, so a real identity provider is a follow-up.
  • The mount-ticket public-key verifier (awcd) uses a single configured key with a fixed validity window of 2020-01-01 through 2100-01-01. Key rotation is not exposed.
  • AWC_CGROUP_ROOTS is read only when the fuse feature is enabled.

docs.title: Error codes and exit codes
docs.text:
This page lists every stable AWC error code, its retryability, and its HTTP status. It then lists the awcctl exit codes from spec Appendix E. The normative source is spec §13.15 and Appendix E.

Clients branch on the stable error code string, not on the human-readable message. The code string never changes form or meaning across releases (spec §13.15).

docs.title: Wire error envelope
docs.text:
Every API error is returned as a JSON document with one error object.

{
  "error": {
    "code": "WRITER_LEASE_HELD",
    "message": "lease held by run-991",
    "request_id": "req_7",
    "retryable": true
  }
}
Field Type Present Meaning code string Always Stable error code in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. Clients branch on this (spec §13.15). message string Always Human-readable detail. Must not contain secrets (spec §19.5). request_id string When set Request id for tracing. Omitted when no id is in scope. retryable boolean Always Whether a retry with backoff may succeed. See the table below.

The request id echoes the x-request-id request header. Mutations also carry an idempotency-key header (spec §13.1).

docs.title: Stable API error codes
docs.text:
The code is authoritative for clients. The HTTP status is advisory. The retryability comes from the classification in the code.

The retryable boolean on the wire reflects the effective retryability for that error instance. A server can override the code default for one instance. Absent an override, the value is the code default listed here.

Code Retryability HTTP status Meaning ALREADY_EXISTS permanent 409 The resource already exists and cannot be recreated. CHECKPOINT_PUBLICATION_FAILED transient 500 Publishing a checkpoint failed. CONTROL_PLANE_UNAVAILABLE transient 503 The control plane is unavailable. HOST_NOT_AUTHORIZED permanent 403 The host is not authorized to act for this workspace. IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT permanent 409 An idempotency key or request conflicts with a prior submission. INVALID_ARGUMENT permanent 422 The request is malformed or semantically invalid. LOCAL_IO_ERROR transient 500 A local I/O error occurred on the host. MOUNT_UNSUPPORTED permanent 422 The requested mount mode is unsupported on this host. NOT_FOUND permanent 404 The referenced resource does not exist. OBJECT_CORRUPT permanent 422 An object failed integrity verification. OBJECT_MISSING permanent 422 A referenced object is missing from the store. OBJECT_STORE_UNAVAILABLE transient 503 The backing object store is unavailable. PERMISSION_DENIED permanent 403 The caller is authenticated but not allowed. QUIESCE_FAILED transient 409 The quiesce required for the operation failed. RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED transient 429 A resource limit (disk, memory, rate) was exhausted. SNAPSHOT_NOT_READY transient 409 The referenced snapshot is not yet in a usable state. STALE_LEASE_GENERATION permanent 409 The supplied lease generation is stale. UNAUTHENTICATED permanent 401 Authentication is missing or invalid. WORKSPACE_BUSY transient 409 The workspace is busy and cannot accept the operation now. WORKSPACE_EXPIRED permanent 410 The workspace TTL has expired. WORKSPACE_VERSION_CONFLICT permanent 409 The workspace optimistic-concurrency version does not match. WRITER_LEASE_HELD transient 409 A writer lease is already held and blocks the operation.

Spec §13.15 requires that errors distinguish retryable from permanent conditions. The spec lists the codes but does not assign the classification. The code is the authority for the retryability column.

docs.title: awcctl retryable HTTP set
docs.text:
The awcctl client retries transient HTTP statuses before it surfaces an error. It is a client policy. The spec does not enumerate it.

HTTP status Retryable Note 408 Yes Request timeout. 425 Yes Too early. 429 Yes Rate limited. Honor Retry-After when present. 5xx except 501, 505 Yes Server-side or data-plane failure. Includes 500, 502, 503, 504. 501 No Not implemented. Permanent. 505 No Version not supported. Permanent. All other 4xx No Caller error. Surface immediately. All 2xx, 3xx No Not an error.

awcctl honors a server Retry-After header, clamped to the backoff cap. The default retry policy bounds retries to three attempts, with an exponential base of 200 ms, a cap of 5 s, and full jitter. The idempotency key on mutations makes a retry safe for POST requests (spec §13.1).

docs.title: awcctl exit codes
docs.text:
Every failure path in awcctl funnels through one error type and exits with one code from spec Appendix E. The table below is the Appendix E contract.

The exit code is a coarse signal. For the exact condition, parse the JSON error document that awcctl --output json prints. That document carries the control-plane code when one is known, plus the matching exit_code.

Code Meaning Retryable 0 Success n/a 2 Invalid command or argument No 3 Authentication or authorization failure No 4 Resource not found No 5 Conflict, busy workspace, or stale version Mixed 6 Local host or mount failure Mixed 7 Object-store or remote I/O failure Mixed 8 Checkpoint or integrity failure Mixed 9 Resource limit exceeded Yes 10 Temporary control-plane unavailability Yes

The Retryable column gives the dominant case. Several exit codes aggregate both transient and permanent error codes. The authoritative retry signal is the retryable boolean in the API error envelope, not the exit code.

docs.title: Error code to exit code mapping
docs.text:
The table below shows which stable error codes map to each non-zero exit code.

Exit code Error codes that map to it 2 INVALID_ARGUMENT, MOUNT_UNSUPPORTED 3 UNAUTHENTICATED, PERMISSION_DENIED, HOST_NOT_AUTHORIZED 4 NOT_FOUND 5 ALREADY_EXISTS, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, SNAPSHOT_NOT_READY, WORKSPACE_EXPIRED, WORKSPACE_BUSY, STALE_LEASE_GENERATION, WORKSPACE_VERSION_CONFLICT, WRITER_LEASE_HELD 6 LOCAL_IO_ERROR 7 OBJECT_MISSING, OBJECT_STORE_UNAVAILABLE 8 OBJECT_CORRUPT, CHECKPOINT_PUBLICATION_FAILED, QUIESCE_FAILED 9 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED 10 CONTROL_PLANE_UNAVAILABLE

CLI-local failures that never carry a control-plane code also map to these exit codes: a bad identifier or a missing option exits 2; a local I/O failure or an unreachable host daemon exits 6; a transport, decode, or object-store failure exits 7; a checkpoint stream that ends without a result exits 8.

docs.title: gRPC status to exit code mapping
docs.text:
The awcd host daemon speaks gRPC. When awcctl receives a gRPC status, it maps the tonic code to an Appendix E exit code.

gRPC code Exit code Ok 0 InvalidArgument, AlreadyExists 2 Unauthenticated, PermissionDenied 3 NotFound 4 Aborted, FailedPrecondition, Cancelled, OutOfRange, DeadlineExceeded 5 Unimplemented, Internal, Unknown, DataLoss 6 ResourceExhausted 9 Unavailable 10

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text:
The error model, the retryability classification, the HTTP status mapping, the JSON envelope, and all Appendix E exit codes are implemented in the current build. Of the 22 stable codes, 15 are constructed by a code path. The remaining 7 — CHECKPOINT_PUBLICATION_FAILED, HOST_NOT_AUTHORIZED, LOCAL_IO_ERROR, MOUNT_UNSUPPORTED, QUIESCE_FAILED, STALE_LEASE_GENERATION, and WORKSPACE_VERSION_CONFLICT — are declared with stable string forms, retryability, HTTP status, and exit-code mappings, but no code path constructs them yet. Their rows in the tables above describe the contract a future emit site must honor; until then a client will not see them on the wire. The HTTP status mapping is the live response status applied by the control plane, with a fallback to 500 if a future code lacks a mapping.

The retryable HTTP set and the retry policy defaults are awcctl client behavior. They are not part of the spec and are not negotiated with the server.

This page verifies the definitions and the mappings. It does not verify that every code is reachable on every endpoint.

docs.title: Fuzz targets
docs.text:
These targets fuzz every untrusted manifest decoder in awc-manifest:

Target Decoder under test decode_canonical awc_manifest::decode (strict canonical CBOR) parse_file FileManifest::from_canonical_bytes parse_tree TreeManifest::from_canonical_bytes parse_snapshot SnapshotManifest::from_canonical_bytes

The targets assert two invariants:

  • decode_canonical requires byte-exact round-trips: any input the strict CBOR decoder accepts must be a fixed point of encode ∘ decode, because canonicality is the whole contract at that layer. The decoder also caps container nesting (128 levels); a hostile deeply-nested input is rejected with NestingTooDeep instead of overflowing the stack.
  • The three manifest parsers require a stable canonical form: parse the input, encode it, parse that again, and both the value and its encoding must be unchanged. The original input need not survive byte-for-byte — unknown fields are ignored and absent optional fields default, by design (spec §21.8 forward compatibility). What must hold is that one pass through parse ∘ encode reaches a fixed point with no information the decoder accepted being lost.

Malformed inputs (non-UTF-8 names, empty or oversized objects, wrong kinds via graph, non-contiguous chunks, invalid digests, unknown enum values, runaway nesting) must be rejected rather than panic.

See on-disk format for the canonical encoding these targets exercise.

docs.title: Seed corpus
docs.text:
Each target starts from a committed seed corpus in fuzz/seeds/<target>/. The seeds are valid manifests and canonical values produced by the crate's own constructors, plus the structured golden vectors hex-decoded from tests/manifests/golden_vectors.json. Regenerate them with the stable toolchain from the repository root:

cargo run -p awc-manifest --example gen_fuzz_seeds

The generator is deterministic: re-running it must leave git status clean. The workspace test suite guards the corpus through crates/awc-manifest/tests/fuzz_seeds.rs, so a seed that stops decoding fails make test before any fuzz run.

fuzz/corpus/<target>/ is the writable directory libFuzzer fills during a run. It is git-ignored; fuzz/seeds/ is committed.

docs.title: Scheduled runs
docs.text: The fuzz workflow runs every target weekly (Monday 04:17 UTC) and on manual dispatch. The nightly toolchain is date-pinned, cargo-fuzz is installed from the stable toolchain, and a dispatch run accepts a max_total_time input (default 300 seconds per target). On failure the job uploads the crash artifacts and the grown corpus as a workflow artifact.

docs.title: Why this is a separate workspace
docs.text: The fuzz crate uses libfuzzer-sys, which requires the nightly toolchain and the sanitizer runtime. It is its own Cargo workspace (note the [workspace] table in Cargo.toml) so that cargo run from the repository root — and therefore make ci — never compiles it. The decoders it targets are otherwise fully covered by the workspace test suite. See Run the test suite.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
cargo +stable install cargo-fuzz --locked   # once
cd fuzz
mkdir -p corpus/decode_canonical
cargo +nightly fuzz run decode_canonical corpus/decode_canonical seeds/decode_canonical

libFuzzer writes new inputs only to the first corpus directory, so fuzz/seeds/ stays untouched. Crash artifacts land under fuzz/artifacts/ (git-ignored). A crash indicates either a non-canonical input that the decoder wrongly accepted or a panic in the decoding path. Either is a correctness bug.

docs.title: Golden test vectors
docs.text: Golden vectors are known-input to known-digest fixtures. They pin the manifest encoding and the content-addressed digest domain for AWC. Every binary that re-derives a digest from a described input must reproduce the recorded digest exactly. The vectors anchor the content-addressing scheme against drift across implementations and releases.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The vectors are a regression guard. A new release runs them to prove that it still emits the same bytes for the same described input. A binary that disagrees with a vector has a format bug.

docs.title: Digest domain
docs.text:
Every vector pins the same domain-separated digest. The digest is taken over a canonical encoding of an object, tagged by its object kind. The object kinds are BLOB, FILE, TREE, and SNAPSHOT. The canonical encoding is defined in on-disk format.

The canonical digest string is sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

docs.title: Release artifacts
docs.text: The golden vectors are checked into the test suite and published as a release artifact. They are versioned independently from the service release version. The fixture is small. Read it from the repository for the exact bytes and digests.

docs.title: Stability contract
docs.text:
A change to a vector is a format change. Three rules follow.

  • The vectors must be checked by all binaries.
  • The format specification and the vectors must be versioned independently from service release versions.
  • Every binary must share the same golden digests.

Do not edit a recorded digest to quiet a failing test. A failing golden test means the encoding changed. Bump the format version and add a new vector set instead.

docs.title: Kernel and filesystem compatibility
docs.text:
This page lists what AWC needs from a Linux host.

The host admission probe gates every entry below. A host that fails an assessed probe is unschedulable for writable mounts.

docs.title: Supported host profile
docs.text:
The certified host profile.

Requirement Value Kernel 6.1 or newer Cgroup hierarchy cgroup v2 FUSE enabled OverlayFS enabled Local filesystem for cache and upper ext4 or XFS xattrs usable Privileges root or equivalent host capabilities for mount management Local storage local SSD or NVMe strongly recommended Network outbound access to the control plane and object store Operating system Linux only (no Windows or macOS mounts)

The daemon reads the kernel release from /proc/sys/kernel/osrelease and parses the leading major.minor. A release below 6.1 fails the probe.

docs.title: Kernel facilities AWC depends on
docs.text: Facility What AWC uses it for OverlayFS Composes the read-only base snapshot (lower) with a private writable delta (upper). FUSE Serves the shared read-only base filesystem. cgroup v2 Freezes the execution cgroup for a quiesced checkpoint. ext4 or XFS Backs the cache and the per-session upper and work directories. xattrs Carries OverlayFS whiteout and opacity markers. Mount namespaces Publishes the merged view to the host, then bind-mounts it into a sandbox. Not a probe category; enforced by the mount helper.

docs.title: OverlayFS mount contract
docs.text:
The workspace overlay is mounted as overlay over three directories:

lowerdir=/var/lib/awc/basefs/tenants/<tenant-id>/snapshots/<root-digest>
upperdir=/var/lib/awc/workspaces/<workspace-id>/<generation>/upper
workdir=/var/lib/awc/workspaces/<workspace-id>/<generation>/work

The mounter shells out to mount -t overlay overlay -o <options> <merged>.

docs.title: Required mount options
docs.text:
AWC disables every OverlayFS behavior that makes checkpoint delta interpretation ambiguous. Each of the following MUST be explicitly off before a workspace is exposed.

Option Required value Reason redirect_dir off Directory redirects would defeat delta interpretation. metacopy off Metadata-only copy-up splits content from metadata. index off Hard-link index adds state AWC does not interpret. xino off Inode remapping is not needed and complicates stable inodes.

AWC rejects any option set where one of these four is absent or set to a value other than off. The mount path checks the policy before it exposes the workspace. Unsupported combinations fail mount creation.

docs.title: OverlayFS delta interpretation
docs.text:
The checkpoint builder scans the upper directory and interprets the kernel's overlay representation. The recognized markers and their xattr namespaces are:

Marker xattr Meaning Whiteout character device 0/0 entry in upper The matching lower entry is deleted. Opaque directory trusted.overlay.opaque=y or user.overlay.opaque=y Lower children of this directory are hidden.

AWC tries user.overlay.opaque first, then trusted.overlay.opaque. An unsupported redirect or metacopy marker causes a safe checkpoint failure, never an incorrect snapshot.

docs.title: Lowerdir path component
docs.text: OverlayFS reserves : as the lowerdir list separator. The lower path component therefore uses a colon-free form: the digest's first colon is replaced with a dash, for example sha256-<hex> instead of sha256:<hex>. The digest keeps its canonical sha256:<hex> form everywhere else.

docs.title: FUSE read-only basefs
docs.text:
One shared read-only FUSE filesystem is mounted at the configured basefs path.

Property Value Mount point /var/lib/awc/basefs (required field, no default) Snapshot path /var/lib/awc/basefs/tenants/<tenant-id>/snapshots/<root-digest>/ Exposed operations lookup, getattr, readdir, open, read, readlink, statfs Write operations Return EROFS Mount options RO, FSName=awc-basefs, AutoUnmount, AllowRoot

There is one multiplexed FUSE daemon per host, not one per workspace.

docs.title: AllowRoot and the overlay-over-FUSE mount
docs.text: The OverlayFS lowerdir points into the FUSE basefs that awcd itself serves. The kernel resolves the lowerdir with root-class credentials. Without AllowRoot, the FUSE mount denies that resolution with EACCES and the overlay mount fails. AllowRoot grants access to root and to the mount owner, which is awcd. This behavior is recorded in the awcd.service capability note.

docs.title: Privileges and capabilities
docs.text:
awcd runs as the unprivileged awc user but holds a fixed, minimal capability set so it can perform privileged mount operations and access /dev/fuse.

Capability Reason CAP_SYS_ADMIN Mount, OverlayFS, bind, cgroup freeze, and setns. CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE Required for the workspace OverlayFS mount whose lowerdir lives in the read-only FUSE basefs. Without it, the kernel's lowerdir resolution fails with EACCES. CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH Checkpoint upper-directory bookkeeping. CAP_CHOWN Per-session upper-directory ownership. CAP_FOWNER Upper-directory file operations.

See systemd units for the full unit. Device access is scoped with DeviceAllow=/dev/fuse rw; PrivateDevices is not set because awcd needs /dev/fuse.

docs.title: Mount namespace visibility
docs.text:
awcd creates the internal merged mount in the host mount namespace, then bind-mounts the path into an authorized sandbox namespace or a configured host target.

The awcd.service unit deliberately omits the systemd directives that create a private mount namespace with disconnected propagation: ProtectSystem, ProtectHome, PrivateTmp, ProtectKernelModules, ProtectKernelLogs, ProtectClock, ProtectProc, and ReadWritePaths. Those directives would confine awcd mounts to a namespace that clients, the worker, and acceptance checks cannot see. Other hardening axes are retained. See systemd units.

docs.title: Namespace target handles
docs.text:
A bind target into a sandbox namespace MUST be identified by a stable, integration-provided handle, never by a raw PID supplied by an untrusted process.

  • A raw PID is rejected as a namespace handle.
  • When a PID is used internally, awcd retains a pidfd-modeled token and re-checks the reuse generation before it enters a namespace or binds.

docs.title: Bind mount hardening
docs.text:
Option Default nodev Always on nosuid Always on noexec Off by default; policy-selected by the sandbox

The inverse options dev and suid are rejected. noexec is off by default because agents may need to run built binaries; the sandbox owns that decision, not the storage layer. The bind target MUST be under an allow-listed root.

docs.title: cgroup v2 quiesce
docs.text:
A quiesced checkpoint freezes the execution cgroup, synchronizes the filesystem, scans a stable delta, publishes, and resumes. The freezer writes and reads the cgroup v2 freeze file.

Operation Action Freeze Write 1 to <cgroup>/cgroup.freeze. Thaw Write 0 to <cgroup>/cgroup.freeze. Confirm frozen Read <cgroup>/cgroup.freeze and poll until 1.

The freeze timeout is bounded by checkpoint.freeze_timeout_seconds (default 10 seconds). The cgroup MUST be below an allow-listed agent subtree, awcd MUST never freeze itself, and a quiesced checkpoint MUST be rejected if the execution group cannot be safely controlled.

docs.title: Host admission probe
docs.text: Before admitting a host for writable mounts, awcd MUST run or verify a compatibility probe. Admission is fail-closed.

docs.title: Registration-time checklist
docs.text:
The full checklist a host MUST pass at registration. Each item names one required FUSE or overlay behavior.

Check name Behavior verified fuse_lower_directory FUSE lower-directory support. file_create_modify_delete_rename_chmod File create, modify, delete, rename, and chmod. symlink_behavior Symlink creation and read. directory_opacity_whiteouts Directory opacity and whiteouts. copy_up_behavior Copy-up from lower to upper. supported_mount_options The AWC option set is accepted. checkpoint_interpretation Delta interpretation matches the live merged view. unmount_cleanup The overlay unmounts cleanly.

A host with every check passing is ACTIVE. Any failure leaves the host UNSCHEDULABLE for writable mounts.

docs.title: Live readiness probe
docs.text:
The /readyz endpoint runs four privilege-free probes on every scrape. They read /proc or /sys and need no capabilities.

The four probes are Kernel, CgroupV2, Fuse, and OverlayFs.

Readiness fails closed on kernel compatibility: an unverified host reports Unknown and /readyz denies new mounts.

docs.title: Probe states and admission decision
docs.text:
A probe result is one of Pass, Fail, or NotAssessed. NotAssessed is distinct from Fail: the host is not known-bad, it is unverified.

Report Admission decision Readiness component Every assessed probe passes Schedulable Ok One or more critical probes could not be assessed Unverified Unknown One or more assessed probes failed Unschedulable Down

The functional probes (rename, chmod, symlink, copy-up, whiteout, opacity, checkpoint interpretation, unmount cleanup) require an overlay mount and therefore CAP_SYS_ADMIN. On an unprivileged host they report NotAssessed rather than Fail, so the host is Unverified, not Unschedulable.

docs.title: Certified tool suite
docs.text:
The tool compatibility suite materializes a snapshot to a real directory and runs one documented operation of each certified tool against it.

Tool Documented operation Git init, add, commit, log. ripgrep Recursive content search. GNU coreutils ls, executable script run, readlink, chmod. Python and pytest A stdlib-only test run. Node.js and a package manager Offline package script run. Rust and Cargo Offline cargo build of a std-only crate. A compiler and linker cc compile and link. Archive tools tar create and extract. A language server Crate indexing.

A tool absent from the environment is skipped, not failed. Network-bound operations are out of scope, so the suite runs offline. The suite proves the materialized tree is byte-, mode-, and symlink-faithful. OverlayFS-specific behavior (whiteouts, copy-up) is verified separately from this suite; a live privileged FUSE mount is out of scope for this suite.

docs.title: Kernel version matrix
docs.text:
A tested kernel matrix is meant to be published with each release. The current repository does not publish that matrix; the only version fact is the minimum floor.

Range Status Reason 6.1 and newer Minimum supported Minimum floor enforced at admission. Below 6.1 Unsupported Fails the admission probe. Specific certified versions Per release Not present in this repository.

A host between the floor and a future certified-version matrix reports Schedulable from the static probes only if it also passes the functional probe. See Current scope.

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text:
What the current build does not yet do:

  • No published kernel matrix. A tested kernel matrix is required per release. The repository ships the minimum floor (6.1) and a probe harness, but no certified-version table.
  • The functional admission probe is privilege-gated. The registration-time checklist is aggregated by the daemon, but the live functional checks that require an overlay mount run only where the daemon has CAP_SYS_ADMIN. On an unprivileged host the functional categories report NotAssessed and the host is Unverified, not Schedulable.
  • No language server is certified in this environment. The language-server slot in the tool suite skips when no functioning server is installed.
  • File watchers are not in the tool suite. Common file watchers are conditional on design-partner need. No watcher test is shipped.
  • The live readiness probe covers four categories. /readyz assesses only Kernel, CgroupV2, Fuse, and OverlayFs. The remaining static probes (UpperFilesystem, Xattrs, MountOptions) and all functional probes are part of the registration-time report, not the per-scrape readiness aggregate. See observability.

docs.title: Limits, quotas, and backpressure
docs.text:
This page lists every limit, quota, and backpressure signal that AWC defines. Each entry names the constant, the default, the knob you tune, and whether the current build enforces it.

Two error classes follow from every limit:

Class Meaning Error code Retry Capacity A shared ceiling is full. Retry after backoff. RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (HTTP 429) Transient Structural The request shape itself is too large. Retry cannot help. INVALID_ARGUMENT (HTTP 422) Permanent

See error codes for the full code set.

docs.title: Disk-pressure state ladder
docs.text:
awcd drives the host through six monotone pressure states as free bytes, free inodes, and PSI stall fractions cross configured thresholds. Containment fires in order: the cheap, safe lever runs first.

Severity State Wire label Containment action 0 Normal NORMAL None. 1 CacheEviction CACHE_EVICTION Reclaim disposable cache objects. 2 PrefetchDisabled PREFETCH_DISABLED Stop speculative prefetch. Demand reads continue. 3 NewMountsDisabled NEW_MOUNTS_DISABLED Reject new writable mounts. 4 UpperWritesAtRisk UPPER_WRITES_AT_RISK Existing upper writes may fail with ENOSPC. Warn agent and platform. 5 Emergency EMERGENCY Only warm reads continue.

Inode scarcity and PSI can only escalate the byte-driven state (take the max). They never relax it. Workspace uppers are never silently deleted; uncheckpointed data is preserved for an operator.

docs.title: Byte thresholds
docs.text:
The five byte thresholds are the free-bytes levels at or below which each state triggers. They must be strictly ordered from mildest to most severe. The daemon derives a correctly spaced ladder from one operator reserve, typically the resolved cache.min_free_bytes.

Threshold Multiplier of the reserve At default reserve (50 GiB) Eviction 3× 150 GiB Prefetch disabled 2× 100 GiB New mounts disabled 1× (equals the reserve) 50 GiB Upper writes at risk 2/3× ~33.3 GiB Emergency 1/3× ~16.7 GiB Checkpoint reserve 1× (the always-preserved floor) 50 GiB

docs.title: Inode and PSI escalators
docs.text:
Input Field Default Effect Free inodes new_mounts_disabled_free_inodes 1024 Free inodes at or below this escalate the state to at least NewMountsDisabled. PSI "some" stall prefetch_disabled_psi_some_bp 5000 bp (50%) Stall at or above this disables prefetch. PSI "full" stall new_mounts_disabled_psi_full_bp 8000 bp (80%) Stall at or above this disables new mounts.

A PSI value of None (the host does not expose /proc/pressure/*) disables that escalator. An inode count of 0 (unknown) is ignored, not treated as scarcity.

docs.title: Reserve enforcement
docs.text:
New writable mounts and checkpoints need the metadata and checkpoint temporary file reserve (checkpoint_reserve_bytes). The reserve admission check tests both the pressure state and the reserve. A refusal returns a visible reserve error that carries the current free bytes, the required reserve, and the pressure state.

Uppers are never deleted to relieve pressure

Cache eviction is the only space-freeing lever. A disk-full condition is surfaced as an error, never papered over by deleting uncheckpointed upper data. See handle disk pressure.

Status: the shipped awcd daemon samples pressure, emits the awc_host_disk_pressure_state gauge, and gates new writable mounts on the reserve check on the host mount path.

docs.title: Cache admission and eviction
docs.text:
The host cache uses a segmented policy that distinguishes one-hit streaming objects, repeatedly accessed hot objects, metadata objects, and explicitly pinned objects. A simple segmented LRU is the current policy; cache-policy learning is deferred.

Eviction order, cheapest first:

  1. one-hit streaming objects (oldest access first);
  2. hot objects (oldest access first);
  3. metadata objects.

Pinned, installing, corrupt, and already-evicted objects are never selected.

Setting Default Purpose Hard byte limit 512 MiB Hard ceiling on total verified bytes. Admission past this triggers eviction. Free-space reserve 2 GiB Minimum free bytes preserved on the cache filesystem. Eviction frees space until this much is available.

Real deployments override both from cache.max_bytes and cache.min_free_bytes (defaults 1 TiB and 50 GiB; see configuration).

Minimum behavior the policy satisfies:

  • enforce a hard byte limit;
  • preserve the configured free-space reserve;
  • prefer evicting old one-hit objects before reused objects;
  • never evict a partially installed object as if it were valid;
  • permit deletion of an object that remains open (Unix file-handle semantics);
  • tombstone the row as Evicted; reconciliation later compacts tombstones.

Status: the policy exists in the library but no call site triggers eviction on admission in the shipped awcd daemon. Cache size is not actively reclaimed by this policy at runtime.

docs.title: Remote-read backpressure
docs.text:
The fetch path bounds remote reads so it never creates unbounded tasks or connections. The admission layer is a concurrency limiter. Every bound is a tokio semaphore, so permit acquisition and drop are cancel-safe.

Setting Default Knob in cache config Bound Global concurrent 64 max_remote_fetches (default 128) Total remote reads in flight across all tenants. Per-tenant concurrent 16 max_remote_fetches_per_tenant (default 32) Remote reads in flight for one tenant. Prefetch concurrent 8 max_prefetch_fetches (default 8) Sub-capacity only prefetch pays. Demand ignores it. Bytes in flight 256 MiB Library default Hard ceiling on bytes admitted to flight at once. Default size reservation 1 MiB Library default Bytes reserved when a fetch size is unknown. Queued miss limit 256 Library default Requests waiting for a permit before new ones are refused.

The config bridge maps the three operator concurrency knobs onto the limiter. A zero value (no remote reads permitted) would deadlock a semaphore, so it is clamped to one permit.

Interactive demand reads take priority over speculative prefetch. Demand waits for room; prefetch is refused (and should retry later) when its reserved concurrency or byte budget is unavailable.

Condition When Who is refused Queue saturated Distinct cold misses exceed the queued miss limit. Any new waiter. Prefetch throttled Prefetch would exceed its reserved concurrency or byte budget. Prefetch only. Demand is never refused this way.

Both conditions are transient. The caller backs off and retries.

Observability counters on the limiter: queued, in_flight, bytes_in_flight, demand_admitted, prefetch_admitted, prefetch_throttled, queued_refused. See metrics.

Status: the limiter exists in the library. The fetch coordinator acquires a permit on each leader fetch only when a limiter is attached. The shipped awcd daemon constructs the coordinator without a limiter, so this bound is dormant at runtime until the daemon attaches one.

docs.title: Host quotas and denial-of-service limits
docs.text:
The host and API operational quota policy uses the limits below. A rate field set to 0 means unlimited.

Setting Default Class Enforced by max_mounts_per_host 256 Capacity awcd active-mount count check on the host mount path. max_mounts_per_tenant 64 Capacity Not enforced by awcd. Deferred to the control-plane mount-ticket path. max_mount_rate_per_second 32 Capacity awcd host mount path rate check. max_mount_burst 64 Capacity awcd host mount path rate check. max_upload_bytes 100 GiB Capacity Per-session ceiling. max_upload_concurrency 8 Capacity Declared. No enforcement helper. max_export_bytes 50 GiB Capacity Export size check. api_rate_per_second 0 (unlimited) Capacity Per-key token bucket. api_burst 0 (unlimited) Capacity Per-key burst allowance.

A 0 for either mount dimension means unlimited for that dimension.

The rate limiter is a per-key (typically tenant) token bucket. Buckets are created lazily and start full. A backwards clock skew never robs tokens; the elapsed term is clamped at zero.

Status: the shipped awcd daemon enforces max_mounts_per_host (direct active-mount count check) and the mount-rate gate (max_mount_rate_per_second / max_mount_burst) on the host mount path. Per-tenant mount counting has no call site in the daemon; per-tenant mount isolation is deferred to the control-plane mount-ticket path.

docs.title: Structural content limits
docs.text:
Structural limits bound the work and storage a single import can demand. They are intrinsic to the import operation. A breach is Structural, so it maps to INVALID_ARGUMENT and is permanent.

Setting Default Bound Path component bytes 255 (POSIX NAME_MAX) Bytes in one filename. Path depth 64 Directory nesting depth. The root is depth 0. Entries per directory tree 100000 Entries in one directory tree. File bytes 64 GiB Logical size of one regular file. Snapshot logical bytes 1 TiB Total logical size of the imported snapshot. Objects per import 5000000 Distinct objects one import may produce.

Status: enforced during import. The depth and entry ceilings mirror the manifest graph budgets.

docs.title: Checkpoint and lease timing
docs.text:
Checkpoint and lease limits are resolved and validated at startup. Startup rejects contradictory or unsafe settings.

Setting Default Validation max_concurrent 4 Must be greater than zero. freeze_timeout_seconds 10 Must be greater than zero. preserve_local_grace_seconds 3600 Must be greater than zero. Setting Default Validation renew_interval_seconds 30 Must be strictly less than expiry_seconds. expiry_seconds 90 Must be greater than renew_interval_seconds. disconnected_grace_seconds 60 Must be greater than zero.

A writer lease carries a monotonically increasing generation fencing token. A host with an older generation may keep local bytes but must not publish a checkpoint. EXPIRED, REVOKED, and RELEASED leases cannot publish.

Status: lease lifecycle is owned by the control plane.

docs.title: Idempotency-key retention
docs.text:
Every mutation API supports an Idempotency-Key header or field. Retrying publication with the same key returns the already published snapshot.

The control plane stores idempotency keys in the idempotency_keys table:

idempotency_keys(
    tenant_id, principal_id, operation, key,
    request_hash, response_blob, state, expires_at,
    primary key(tenant_id, principal_id, operation, key)
)

Each row carries an expires_at. Local checkpoint state also records phases and idempotency keys for interrupted-checkpoint recovery.

Status: no operator-facing retention knob is defined; the retention period is implementation-owned.

docs.title: Per-tenant and per-project boundaries
docs.text:
Boundary Mechanism Status Mount count per host Active-mount count check (max_mounts_per_host). Enforced by awcd on the host mount path. Mount count per tenant Per-tenant mount counter (max_mounts_per_tenant). Not enforced by awcd; deferred to the control-plane mount-ticket path. Remote reads per tenant Per-tenant semaphore (max_remote_fetches_per_tenant). Implemented; dormant in awcd (the limiter is not attached to the coordinator). API request rate per tenant Per-key token bucket (api_rate_per_second, api_burst). Implemented; not wired per-tenant at runtime. Defaults to unlimited. Upper-directory bytes and inodes Filesystem project quotas or dedicated filesystem quotas. Operator-provided. AWC recommends them and does not enforce a counter. Cross-tenant cache deduplication Forbidden. Objects are namespaced under objects/<tenant>/. Enforced by the cache layout.

Per-tenant concurrency and bandwidth controls should be implemented in the daemon. A malicious workspace must not exhaust host disk and take down unrelated tenants.

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text:
This page distinguishes what the code implements from what the shipped daemon enforces at runtime.

Implemented in library code (the enforcement logic exists):

  • The disk-pressure state machine, the reserve check, and the visible reserve error.
  • The segmented-LRU cache admission, eviction, and pinning policy.
  • The remote-read backpressure limiter and the config bridge.
  • The host quota primitives: mount counting, rate limiting, and upload and export size checks.
  • Checkpoint, lease, and cache limit resolution and validation.

Enforced at runtime:

  • Disk-pressure sampling, the awc_host_disk_pressure_state gauge, and the reserve gate on the host mount path.
  • max_mounts_per_host via a direct active-mount count check, and the mount-rate gate (max_mount_rate_per_second, max_mount_burst), both on the host mount path.
  • Structural content limits on the import path.

Implemented but dormant at runtime in awcd:

  • The eviction policy. No call site triggers eviction on admission, so the cache size is not actively reclaimed by this policy in the shipped daemon.
  • The remote-read concurrency limiter. The fetch coordinator acquires a permit only when a limiter is attached; awcd constructs the coordinator without one, so the bound is inactive.

Declared, with no library helper and no awcd call site:

  • max_upload_concurrency.
  • max_upload_bytes and max_export_bytes.
  • max_mounts_per_tenant. Per-tenant mount isolation is deferred to the control-plane mount-ticket path.

Not configurable in the documented configuration block (library defaults only):

  • Bytes in flight, default size reservation, and queued miss limit.
  • The idempotency-key retention period.

Specified, deferred (not implemented):

  • Cache-policy learning, content-defined chunking, and learned prefetch are deferred, not implemented.

docs.title: Metrics reference
docs.text:
AWC exposes a bounded Prometheus-style metrics registry. Instrument names are defined by the telemetry module. This page reflects what the current build records.

Two registries ship: one in the awcd host daemon, one in the awc-worker job runner. Only awcd exposes a /metrics endpoint (see Scrape endpoint); awc-worker records into its registry but serves no HTTP, so its metrics are not scrapeable in this build.

docs.title: Cardinality model
docs.text: The registry caps distinct label-sets per instrument at 128. A recording that would add a new label-set beyond the cap rolls into the synthetic value cardinality_overflow instead of being dropped. Use closed-set label values only. Do not put a path, digest, workspace ID, or tenant ID in a label. The primary backend forbids these.

docs.title: Emitted metrics
docs.text:
Every row below has a real recording site in non-test code. A declared name alone is not enough to qualify.

Name Type Labels Binary Meaning awc_workspace_mounts_total counter none awcd Adds one for each accepted workspace mount. awc_workspace_unmounts_total counter none awcd Adds one for each workspace unmount. awc_workspace_active_mounts gauge none awcd Current count of active mount sessions. Set to 0 at start. awc_workspace_checkpoint_total counter outcome awcd Adds one at each checkpoint stream terminal event. awc_host_disk_pressure_state gauge none awcd Host disk-pressure severity rank, 0..=5. Sampled every 5 s. See pressure ranks. awc_host_free_bytes gauge none awcd Free bytes on the filesystem holding the cache. Sampled every 5 s. awc_host_free_inodes gauge none awcd Free inodes on that filesystem. Sampled every 5 s. awc_host_upper_usage_bytes gauge none awcd Bytes held in uncheckpointed upper directories. Sampled every 5 s. awc_host_cache_bytes gauge none awcd (fuse feature) Total verified bytes in the cache index. Sampled every 30 s. awc_cache_hits_total counter none awcd (fuse feature) Reads served from a verified cached object. Folded every 5 s. awc_cache_misses_total counter none awcd (fuse feature) Read passes that went to the singleflight path. Folded every 5 s. awc_singleflight_leader_fetches_total counter none awcd (fuse feature) Cumulative singleflight leader fetches. Folded from the fetch coordinator every 5 s. awc_singleflight_follower_requests_total counter none awcd (fuse feature) Cumulative singleflight follower requests. Folded every 5 s. awc_fuse_request_duration_seconds histogram op awcd (fuse feature) Wall-clock duration of one served FUSE request, recorded at completion. awc_fuse_inflight_requests gauge none awcd (fuse feature) FUSE requests currently being served. Sampled every 5 s; set to 0 at start. awc_lease_renewal_failures_total counter none awcd Lease-bearing sessions whose renewal RPC failed. Counted per renewal pass. awc_background_jobs_total counter kind, outcome awc-worker Adds one for each processed background job. awc_background_job_lag_seconds gauge kind awc-worker Ready-to-processed lag for the most recent job of each kind, in seconds. awc_api_errors_total counter component=worker awc-worker Adds one for each transient worker store error. awc_snapshot_validation_duration_seconds histogram outcome awc-worker Wall-clock duration of one snapshot validation. awc_workspace_forks_total counter none awc-control Adds the batch size for each committed workspace fork. Idempotent replays do not count. awc_active_writer_leases gauge none awc-control Live writer leases (issued, active, or releasing, and unexpired). Sampled every 15 s; set to 0 at start.

Label value sets:

  • awc_workspace_checkpoint_total outcome: one of published, failed, cancelled.
  • awc_background_jobs_total kind: the job's kind string from the job row.
  • awc_background_jobs_total outcome: one of completed, failed, cancelled, retried, other.
  • awc_api_errors_total component: the fixed value worker.
  • awc_snapshot_validation_duration_seconds outcome: one of validated, invalid, skipped, error.
  • awc_fuse_request_duration_seconds op: one of lookup, getattr, read, readdir, readlink, statfs.

The singleflight and cache counters are gated behind the fuse build feature. The sampler reads cumulative counters from the fetch coordinator and folds their deltas into the registry. The FUSE instruments share that gate: awc_fuse_request_duration_seconds is recorded directly in the FUSE mount thread as each request completes, and awc_fuse_inflight_requests is folded by the 5 s sampler.

A cache miss counts one per get_or_fetch pass that reaches the singleflight path, not per RPC: a pass whose leader died and retried counts one miss, and if the retry finds the object verified it also counts one hit. Hits and misses therefore do not sum to a request count.

The free-space gauges come from the newest successful probe sample. A probe that keeps failing leaves the last value in place. awc_lease_renewal_failures_total counts sessions, not passes: one pass over two unreachable sessions adds two.

Singleflight counters are a cross-host signal

On one loopback host, the local cache fast-path serves a repeat read before a second request joins the in-flight fetch. Expect awc_singleflight_follower_requests_total to stay at 0 in single-host traffic. The counters measure cross-host coalescing, where two hosts race for the same missing object.

docs.title: Pressure ranks
docs.text:
awc_host_disk_pressure_state records the pressure severity as an integer. The states escalate monotonically.

Value State 0 NORMAL 1 CACHE_EVICTION 2 PREFETCH_DISABLED 3 NEW_MOUNTS_DISABLED 4 UPPER_WRITES_AT_RISK 5 EMERGENCY

docs.title: Declared but not emitted
docs.text:
Every row below is declared in the telemetry module but has no recording site in shipped code. Each stays unemitted for a concrete reason:

Name Type Intended meaning Why it is not emitted awc_workspace_checkpoint_uploaded_bytes counter Unique bytes a checkpoint uploads. The checkpoint result reports zeros for the upload/reuse split today; emitting them would lie. Lands with a CheckpointStats split. awc_workspace_checkpoint_reused_bytes counter Bytes a checkpoint reuses from prior objects. Same as above: the split does not exist in the stats yet. awc_host_cache_evictions_total counter Cache evictions. No shipped binary invokes the eviction policy. awc_host_cache_corruption_total counter Detected cache corruption events. No shipped binary runs cache reconcile (the corruption detector) on a schedule.

Notes on this table:

  • The declared histogram bucket upper bounds are 0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.5, 5.0, 10.0 seconds.
  • The metric catalog lists more names than the code declares (for example awc_read_logical_bytes_total, awc_workspace_mount_duration_seconds, awc_snapshot_logical_bytes). Those have no declared constant and no recording site. They are omitted here.

docs.title: Scrape endpoint
docs.text:
GET /metrics on the awcd health HTTP listener returns the Prometheus text exposition. The same listener serves three routes:

Route Returns GET /healthz Liveness. 200 when the process is up. GET /readyz Readiness for new writable mounts. Preserves the warm-read flag. GET /metrics Prometheus text exposition.

The listener is off by default. The host API stays on its Unix-domain socket; only health and metrics use the HTTP listener.

Knob Where Value Config file key health_http_listen A loopback host:port, for example 127.0.0.1:9100. Environment variable AWC_HEALTH_HTTP_LISTEN Same format as the file key. Type Option<SocketAddr> Optional. Default None The listener is not started.

awcd starts the listener only when health_http_listen is set. The value must parse as a host:port, or awcd returns a config error.

awc-control serves GET /metrics on its REST listener (AWC_CONTROL_LISTEN), alongside /v1/health. The route is unauthenticated, like the liveness probe: bind the listener to a private interface. It exposes the two awc-control rows above. A failed lease sample keeps the last gauge value and logs.

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text:
What the current build does not yet do:

  • The FUSE instruments cover the six read-path operations only (lookup, getattr, read, readdir, readlink, statfs). Other kernel callbacks, including the mutating operations that reply EROFS, are not timed.
  • Cache eviction and corruption have no recording sites. awc_host_cache_evictions_total and awc_host_cache_corruption_total stay unset until a binary schedules eviction and reconcile.
  • Only a Prometheus text exposition is implemented. An OTLP exporter is not layered on. The render path is the integration point for one.
  • awc-worker records its metrics (awc_background_jobs_total, awc_background_job_lag_seconds, awc_api_errors_total, awc_snapshot_validation_duration_seconds) into an in-process registry but starts no HTTP listener. These counters have no /metrics scrape target in this build; wire them to an exporter before relying on them.

docs.title: Observability reference
docs.text: The operator surfaces of AWC are the awcd health HTTP endpoints, the /metrics scrape, structured logs, traces, and the audit-event log.

docs.title: Health HTTP endpoints
docs.text:
awcd serves three HTTP/1.1 routes on a separate loopback listener. The host API stays on its Unix-domain gRPC socket; only health and metrics use this listener.

Route Method Returns HTTP 200 HTTP 503 /healthz GET Liveness plus the full report body The process is up and the base filesystem is serving. A foundational component is hard-down. /readyz GET Readiness for new writable mounts plus the full report body The host can accept a new writable mount. The host cannot accept a new writable mount. Warm reads may still be served. /metrics GET Prometheus text exposition Always, when the listener is up. Never.

Any other method returns 405. Any other path returns 404. Both /healthz and /readyz return the same JSON body, a HealthReport. Only the status code differs.

The listener is opt-in. When health_http_listen is unset, the HTTP server does not start and GetHostStatus is the only host-status surface (over gRPC).

Knob Where Value Config key health_http_listen A loopback host:port, for example 127.0.0.1:9100. Env var AWC_HEALTH_HTTP_LISTEN Same format. Type Option<SocketAddr> The listener address is optional. Default unset The listener is not started.

The value must parse as a host:port or awcd returns a config error. It should be a loopback address so the endpoints are not exposed broadly. See configuration and environment variables.

docs.title: Health report body
docs.text:
/healthz and /readyz return a JSON HealthReport.

Field Type Meaning live bool Liveness. The process is up and its event loop makes progress. ready_for_new_mounts bool The host can accept a new writable mount. warm_read_ready bool The host can keep serving existing warm reads. components array One object per component. See components.

Each components entry has three fields:

Field Type Meaning name string A canonical component name. See components. state string One of ok, degraded, down, unknown. See component states. detail string or null A closed-set, non-sensitive verdict, for example active_mounts=2.

docs.title: Health components
docs.text:
awcd derives the report from seven components.

Component name State in the current build Base filesystem base_fuse ok when mounted, degraded while mounting or unmounting, down otherwise Cache cache ok Kernel compatibility kernel_compat ok, degraded, or unknown Mounts and leases mounts_leases ok Control plane control_plane unknown Object store object_store unknown Disk pressure disk_pressure ok, degraded, down, or unknown

docs.title: Component states
docs.text:
Each component state has one of four values. They serialize in snake_case.

State Meaning ok Healthy or nominal. degraded Serving but impaired. For example, elevated disk pressure. down Required for readiness and currently failing. unknown Not yet probed. The transport for this build is not wired.

docs.title: Readiness model
docs.text:
A host may stay ready for existing warm reads while it is unready for new writable mounts. The report preserves that distinction.

Flag Derived rule live base_fuse is not down. warm_read_ready base_fuse and cache are ok or degraded. ready_for_new_mounts warm_read_ready and kernel_compat is ok or degraded, and mounts_leases, disk_pressure, control_plane, and object_store are not down.

/healthz returns 200 when live is true. /readyz returns 200 only when ready_for_new_mounts is true. For kernel_compat, unknown fails readiness closed: an unverified kernel is not admitted. The mounts_leases, disk_pressure, control_plane, and object_store gates fail readiness only when down, not when unknown.

Because the readiness rule for control_plane and object_store is not_down, their unknown state does not by itself fail /readyz. In the shipped binary kernel_compat is wired to the live probe, so on a schedulable, non-pressured host /readyz returns 200 even while those two components report unknown. A real down connectivity verdict cannot be asserted until the probes are wired. Warm reads still return 200 on the liveness probe.

docs.title: Disk pressure states
docs.text:
The disk_pressure component maps a pressure state to a component state. States escalate monotonically by severity rank.

Rank State string Component state Effect 0 NORMAL ok No containment. 1 CACHE_EVICTION degraded Disposable cache is evicted. 2 PREFETCH_DISABLED degraded Speculative prefetch yields. 3 NEW_MOUNTS_DISABLED down New writable mounts are rejected. 4 UPPER_WRITES_AT_RISK down Existing uppers may hit ENOSPC. 5 EMERGENCY down Only warm reads continue.

The detail string for disk_pressure is state=<STATE>; uncheckpointed_upper_bytes=<n>. The monitor never silently deletes uncheckpointed upper data to relieve pressure. The rank is also exported as the awc_host_disk_pressure_state metric. See metrics.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
GET /metrics returns a Prometheus-style text exposition. The registry caps distinct label-sets per instrument at 128. Recordings beyond the cap roll into the synthetic value cardinality_overflow. Do not put a path, digest, workspace ID, or tenant ID in a label.

awcd serves /metrics on its health HTTP listener (see above). awc-control serves /metrics on its REST listener, alongside /v1/health; that route is unauthenticated, so bind the listener to a private interface.

The full metric catalog, the label sets, the emitted-versus-declared split, and the histogram buckets are on the metrics reference page.

docs.title: Structured logs
docs.text:
Logs are structured JSON lines that carry a request or operation ID.

Field Type Meaning op_id string The request or operation id. level string One of INFO, WARN, ERROR. message string A short event summary. fields object Closed-set, non-sensitive facts. For example, a stage name or a count. ts string The event timestamp, RFC 3339, UTC.

A deployment wires an event sink for the events. Two sinks ship: one writes a JSON line per event to standard error; one collects lines in memory for in-process tests. Logs should record state transitions, not every successful file read.

Under systemd, all three units send standard output and standard error to journald (StandardOutput=journal, StandardError=journal). Tail with journalctl -u awcd -f. See systemd units.

The following must never appear in a log line:

  • file contents;
  • access tokens;
  • object-store credentials;
  • raw secret-bearing paths.

Redact a path before you log it. See tracing and redaction.

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text:
A trace should connect the workspace operation to the object-store request and the publication transaction.

workspace operation
  -> mount ticket
  -> host mount preparation
  -> FUSE lookup/read
  -> cache lookup
  -> singleflight wait
  -> object-store request
  -> checkpoint quiesce
  -> object upload
  -> publication transaction

Trace attributes may include tenant, project, host, snapshot digest, workspace ID, cache outcome, object size, and error class. File paths must be redacted or hashed by default because they may contain sensitive information.

The redaction behavior is as follows.

Operation Input Output Path redaction A path and a keep_depth awc:<head>:<hash>. The first keep_depth components are kept; the rest collapses to a short SHA-256 hash. Secret redaction Any secret-bearing string The fixed placeholder awc:redacted:secret. ID hashing Any text sha256: plus the first eight bytes of the SHA-256 digest, in lower-case hex.

An OpenTelemetry-compatible OTLP exporter is not layered on. The metrics registry render path is the integration point for one. See Current scope.

docs.title: Audit events
docs.text: The control plane records immutable audit events for privileged mutations. Each event is one row in the append-only audit_events table. The action and resource_type columns use a fixed set of values so the log stays greppable by category.

docs.title: audit_events table
docs.text:
The table schema is as follows.

Column Type Meaning id bigserial Row primary key. tenant_id TEXT The tenant the event belongs to. principal_id TEXT, nullable The actor. A system principal for background passes. action TEXT The action string. See actions. resource_type TEXT The resource family. See resource types. resource_id TEXT The resource identifier. request_id TEXT, nullable The inbound request id, when one is in scope. detail jsonb Actor, resource, request, and state-transition facts. created_at timestamptz The event time.

The detail column records only identifiers, digests, counts, and enum verdicts. It must not contain object contents, byte payloads, manifest bodies, file names from user data, credentials, tokens, or keys.

docs.title: Audit actions
docs.text:
Every action follows the <resource>.<verb> shape. The table below lists each action constant and its string value.

Constant action value CHECKPOINT_PUBLISH checkpoint.publish WORKSPACE_EXPIRE workspace.expire WORKSPACE_DELETE workspace.delete SNAPSHOT_MARK_DELETING snapshot.mark_deleting SNAPSHOT_CREATE snapshot.create SNAPSHOT_TRANSITION snapshot.transition SNAPSHOT_SCRUB snapshot.scrub GC_SWEEP gc.sweep HOST_REGISTER host.register HOST_REVOKE host.revoke HOST_ROTATE host.rotate HOST_COMPATIBILITY host.compatibility IMPORT_SESSION_CREATE import_session.create SIGNING_KEY_ROTATE signing_key.rotate SIGNING_KEY_RETIRE signing_key.retire SIGNING_KEY_REVOKE signing_key.revoke OBJECT_CREDENTIAL_ISSUE object_credential.issue

docs.title: Audit resource types
docs.text:
The resource_type column takes these values.

Constant resource_type value Status WORKSPACE workspace Emitted. SNAPSHOT snapshot Emitted. IMPORT_SESSION import_session Emitted. HOST host Emitted. GC_RUN gc_run Emitted. SIGNING_KEY signing_key Emitted. OBJECT_CREDENTIAL object_credential Emitted. LEASE lease Reserved. No action is emitted. MOUNT_SESSION mount_session Reserved. No action is emitted. EXPORT export Reserved. No action is emitted.

docs.title: System principals
docs.text:
Background passes record a system principal in principal_id.

Constant principal_id value Pass RETENTION system:retention The retention and TTL pass. GC system:gc The durable garbage collector. VALIDATION system:validation The closure-validation job. SCRUB system:scrub The durable-object integrity scrub.

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text:
What the current build does not yet do:

  • Connectivity probes are not wired. The control_plane and object_store components report unknown. Their readiness gate is not_down, so unknown does not by itself fail /readyz; on a schedulable, non-pressured host /readyz still returns 200. A real down verdict for connectivity cannot be asserted until the probes are wired. The cache reports ok with the detail corruption probe not wired.
  • Tracing is not exported. The redaction helpers are available, and the span chain is the target shape, but no OTLP exporter is wired. The metrics render path is the integration point.
  • Several audit categories have no emit site. The reserved LEASE, MOUNT_SESSION, and EXPORT resource types have no actions. Events are required for writer lease acquisition, revocation, and expiration; mount ticket issuance; mount and unmount; export; retention-policy changes; administrative recovery; and authorization failures for privileged operations. None of these are emitted yet. Workspace creation and fork also have no dedicated action.
  • Two histograms are recorded. awc_snapshot_validation_duration_seconds is recorded by awc-worker (no HTTP listener, so not scrapeable). awc_fuse_request_duration_seconds is recorded by awcd per served FUSE request (fuse feature). See metrics.
  • Many metrics are declared but not emitted. See the declared-not-emitted table on the metrics reference page.

docs.title: On-disk format
docs.text: This page describes how immutable content-addressed storage (CAS) objects are serialized and named. The format lets AWC deduplicate, verify, and share objects across hosts.

docs.title: 1. Object identity
docs.text:
Every immutable object is named by an algorithm-qualified digest, shown as:

sha256:<64 lowercase hexadecimal characters>

The digest mixes a version tag and the object kind into the hash. This domain separation means the same byte payload can never be read as two object kinds. A blob, a file, a tree, and a snapshot that share the same bytes still get distinct names.

Two objects are identical if and only if they share the same object kind and the same canonical payload. The digest captures exactly that.

docs.title: 2. Canonical encoding
docs.text:
Structured objects use a deterministic canonical CBOR encoding as defined by RFC 8949:

  • Definite lengths only. Every byte string, text string, array, and map carries a definite length. Indefinite-length encodings are forbidden.
  • Shortest forms. Integers and lengths use the shortest available encoding.
  • Sorted map keys. Map entries are ordered by the bytewise comparison of the encoded key.
  • No duplicate keys within a single map.

Deterministic encoding keeps the serialized bytes stable, so the same logical object produces the same digest on every host.

docs.title: 3. Object kinds
docs.text:
AWC stores four object kinds:

  • BLOB — raw bytes. The canonical payload is the blob itself.
  • FILE — file metadata plus references to one or more content blobs. Small files reference a single blob. Larger files are split into chunks, each stored as its own blob. The logical file digest covers the complete file bytes. It is independent of how the file is chunked.
  • TREE — a directory listing of named child entries. Entries are sorted lexicographically by raw name bytes. Names must be non-empty and must not contain path separators or NUL bytes. Each entry names a child file, tree, or symlink by its digest.
  • SNAPSHOT — a pointer to a root tree, provenance and metadata, and an optional parent snapshot. Mutable control-plane state, such as human-readable names and retention policy, points at a snapshot record. It is not part of the snapshot's content identity.

docs.title: 4. Forward compatibility
docs.text: Every serialized manifest carries a version field, and the digest domain carries a version tag. Future hash algorithms or structural changes can be introduced by bumping the tag. The tag keeps new objects distinct from existing ones.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Data model — identifiers, object kinds, and the workspace, lease, ticket, and patch-bundle records that reference these objects.
  • Golden vectors — the versioned manifest test vectors.
  • Fuzz targets — the encode ∘ decode fixed-point fuzzers.

docs.title: Retention and garbage collection reference
docs.text:
Durable garbage collection (GC) reclaims content-addressed objects that no retained root can reach. It runs as one mark-and-sweep epoch over a single tenant. For the operational runbook, see Run garbage collection.

GC targets the durable object store only. It does not evict from the host cache.

docs.title: The epoch
docs.text:
One epoch is the unit of work. The handler gc_sweep drives it end to end. The table maps each phase to its action.

Step Phase What happens 1 Roots Read the manifest digests of every READY snapshot for the tenant. 2 Mark Traverse the object graph from the roots.
