Collect every reachable digest. 3 Inventory Enumerate every object the store holds for the tenant. 4 Plan Diff the inventory against the marked set under the grace cutoff. 4b Holds Remove candidates pinned by an integrity hold. 5 Record Write one CANDIDATE row per candidate digest. 6 Sweep Delete candidates in bounded batches with a leading canary. 7 Mark deleted Flip physically removed rows to DELETED. 8 Complete Record the counts and the summary on the epoch row. 9 Audit Append one gc.sweep audit event.

A failed epoch deletes nothing. See Failure behavior.

docs.title: Retained roots
docs.text:
The mark phase roots at two sources only:

Root source How it protects content Manifest digest of every READY snapshot Traversal reaches its trees, files, file-chunk blobs, and symlink blobs. Digests pinned in gc_integrity_holds Removed from the candidate set before the sweep. Protects the closure of a snapshot degraded by a missing or corrupt object.

The SQL for the READY roots is one query:

SELECT manifest_digest FROM snapshots
WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND state = 'READY';

More roots are live than the epoch marks: a workspace base or head, a retained checkpoint alias, an active import session, an active export job, a legal hold, a GC grace record, and an administrative pin. The current build does not mark from those directly. Objects they reference stay safe through the grace cutoff when their age beats the cutoff.

Narrow root gap

An import that runs longer than AWC_GC_GRACE_SECS without producing a READY snapshot has its uploaded objects protected by timestamp alone. Finish long imports before you sweep, or raise the grace for the run.

docs.title: Candidate eligibility
docs.text:
An object becomes a deletion candidate when both conditions hold.

Condition Rule Edge case Unreachable The digest is absent from the marked set. None. Grace-expired created_at is set and is strictly before the cutoff (now - safety_grace). An object created exactly at the cutoff is protected. Unknown age created_at is None. Never a candidate. The sweep is conservative about anything it cannot age.

docs.title: Safety grace
docs.text:
The grace protects an object uploaded by a concurrent import or checkpoint whose root snapshot has not yet reached READY and been observed by this epoch.

Item Value Cutoff now - AWC_GC_GRACE_SECS Default 86400 seconds (24 hours) Stored on gc_runs.cutoff Comparison Strictly before. Equal is protected.

The epoch records the cutoff it used. An object uploaded after the roots were snapshotted is protected by timestamp even when it is not yet reachable.

docs.title: Integrity holds
docs.text:
An integrity hold pins one digest against GC for one tenant. It fences the sweep around a degraded snapshot's recovery content.

Property Value Storage PostgreSQL table gc_integrity_holds. Survives worker restarts. Producer The scrub path. It pins the closure of a degraded snapshot, then releases it after restore. Read by sweep Held digests are removed from the candidate set before the sweep. Failure mode If holds cannot be read, the epoch is recorded FAILED. Nothing is deleted. Tenant scope One tenant. No cross-tenant leak.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The worker reads these variables once at startup. Restart the worker when you change one.

Variable Type Default Meaning AWC_GC_GRACE_SECS integer 86400 Safety grace in seconds. Objects newer than now - grace are never swept. AWC_GC_BATCH_SIZE integer 1000 Max candidates one epoch deletes across all batches. Bounds each run as a canary. AWC_GC_CANARY_SIZE integer 10 Size of the leading batch inside an epoch. AWC_GC_DRY_RUN string unset Plan only, delete nothing. Truthy values are 1, true, and TRUE.

The knobs are environment-wide, not per tenant. A per-project retention policy is prospective and does not drive the sweep in this build.

docs.title: Sweep batching
docs.text:
The sweep deletes candidates in batches.

Batch Cap First batch (canary) min(AWC_GC_CANARY_SIZE, remaining) Later batches min(AWC_GC_BATCH_SIZE, remaining) Total per epoch min(AWC_GC_BATCH_SIZE, candidate_count)

Candidates not deleted this epoch are pending. They are left for a subsequent epoch. The run reports the pending count in the job result.

docs.title: Dry run
docs.text: Set AWC_GC_DRY_RUN=1 to plan candidates and record them without deleting anything. In a dry run every candidate stays in state CANDIDATE, deleted_count is 0, and every candidate is reported pending.

docs.title: Database tables
docs.text: Three tables record the durable-GC accounting.

docs.title: gc_runs
docs.text:
One row per epoch (migration 20260807000003_gc_runs.sql).

Column Type Notes epoch bigserial PRIMARY KEY Monotonic epoch id. tenant_id TEXT NOT NULL References tenants(id), cascades on delete. cutoff timestamptz NOT NULL Objects newer than this are grace-protected. state TEXT NOT NULL RUNNING, COMPLETED, or FAILED. dry_run boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false Whether this epoch deleted anything. roots_count bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 Retained roots snapshotted. marked_count bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 Digests reached by the mark phase. inventory_count bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 Objects enumerated from the store. candidate_count bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 Unreachable and grace-expired. deleted_count bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 Physically removed this epoch. reclaimed_bytes bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 Bytes reclaimed this epoch. summary jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}' Per-kind counts and run config. See Run summary. error TEXT Set when state = FAILED. started_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() Epoch start. completed_at timestamptz Epoch completion.

Index: gc_runs_tenant_started_idx on (tenant_id, started_at DESC).

State transitions:

From To Trigger (new row) RUNNING The epoch opens. RUNNING COMPLETED The counts are written. RUNNING FAILED The error column is written.

docs.title: gc_deletion_plans
docs.text:
One row per candidate digest in an epoch (migration 20260807000003_gc_runs.sql).

Column Type Notes epoch bigint NOT NULL References gc_runs(epoch), cascades on delete. tenant_id TEXT NOT NULL References tenants(id), cascades on delete. digest TEXT NOT NULL Canonical sha256:<hex>. kind TEXT NOT NULL BLOB, FILE, TREE, or SNAPSHOT. size_bytes bigint NOT NULL Object size. state TEXT NOT NULL CANDIDATE, DELETED, or SKIPPED. created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() Plan row creation.

Primary key: (epoch, digest). Index: gc_deletion_plans_tenant_state_idx on (tenant_id, state).

State transitions in the current write path:

From To Trigger (new row) CANDIDATE One row is inserted per candidate. CANDIDATE DELETED After the physical delete.

The schema permits SKIPPED. The current write path does not set it.

docs.title: gc_integrity_holds
docs.text:
One row per pinned digest per tenant (migration 20260807000004_gc_integrity_holds.sql).

Column Type Notes tenant_id TEXT NOT NULL References tenants(id), cascades on delete. digest TEXT NOT NULL Canonical sha256:<hex>. created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() Hold creation.

Primary key: (tenant_id, digest). Index: gc_integrity_holds_tenant_idx on (tenant_id).

docs.title: Audit events
docs.text:
One audit event is appended per epoch.

Field Value Action gc.sweep Resource kind gc_run Resource id The epoch id, as a string. Principal GC_PRINCIPAL

The detail payload records the run outcome:

Key Meaning cutoff The grace cutoff timestamp used. dry_run Whether this was a dry run. candidate_count Candidates after holds were applied. deleted_count Candidates physically deleted. reclaimed_bytes Bytes reclaimed. held_blocked Candidates removed because a hold pinned them.

docs.title: Run summary
docs.text:
The gc_runs.summary JSON column stores per-kind candidate counts and the run config.

Key Meaning candidate_bytes Sum of candidate size_bytes. by_kind.BLOB Candidate count of kind BLOB. by_kind.FILE Candidate count of kind FILE. by_kind.TREE Candidate count of kind TREE. by_kind.SNAPSHOT Candidate count of kind SNAPSHOT. safety_grace_secs The grace used, in seconds. batch_size The run cap used. canary_batch_size The canary size used.

The job result carries the same counts plus pending_count.

docs.title: Failure behavior
docs.text:
The mark phase aborts on the first traversal inconsistency. A failed epoch is recorded FAILED with its reason in gc_runs.error, and nothing is deleted.

Variant Meaning MissingObject A referenced object is absent mid-traversal. KindMismatch A referenced object's stored kind does not match its referencer. MalformedObject An object failed to parse as its declared kind. OversizedObject A single object exceeded the per-object byte budget. OversizedTree A tree exceeded the maximum entry count. ExcessiveDepth Tree nesting exceeded the depth budget. Store The object store failed a fetch or a delete. Inventory The object store failed to enumerate its inventory. InvalidRoot A retained-root manifest digest was not well-formed. Db A control-plane (PostgreSQL) failure.

The gc_sweep handler maps errors to job outcomes. A missing or blank tenant_id in the payload fails the job permanently. Any epoch error retries, because the run is idempotent. A genuine reachability inconsistency records a FAILED epoch each attempt and dead-letters once max_attempts is exhausted.

docs.title: Retention policy
docs.text:
A project retention policy defines these prospective fields:

default workspace TTL
checkpoint retention duration
failed import retention
preserved-local grace
export retention
minimum GC grace
legal-hold behavior

Retention changes apply prospectively unless an administrator explicitly requests re-evaluation of existing resources. The current build does not drive the sweep from a retention policy.

docs.title: Local cache GC
docs.text: Host-local cache eviction is independent from durable GC. Cache entries may be removed at any time if they are not being installed and local readers tolerate normal Unix unlink semantics. Local workspace uppers are deleted only after a successful unmount disposition, lease release or fencing, no active bind mounts, the configured recovery grace, and confirmation that no checkpoint operation still references the directory.

docs.title: Cross-links
docs.text:
• Run garbage collection — the operational runbook.
  • Environment variables — the AWC_GC_* knobs.
  • Database schema — the full schema.
  • Error codes — error surfaces.

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text:
The GC engine is complete and unit-tested. These items are specified but not present in the current build, or lag the spec:

  • No awcctl gc command. Run GC by enqueuing a gc_sweep job into the PostgreSQL job queue with an awc-worker process running to claim it.
  • No GC auto-scheduler. The control plane enqueues snapshot_validate on import, but it never enqueues gc_sweep. You must trigger each epoch by hand.
  • The storage gauges are not emitted. awc_tenant_unreachable_grace_bytes, awc_tenant_unique_durable_bytes, and awc_snapshot_logical_bytes are specified but are not emitted. Measure unreachable bytes with a dry-run epoch, not with a gauge.
  • GC knobs are environment-wide, not per tenant. The AWC_GC_* variables apply to every tenant the worker serves. A per-project retention policy does not drive the sweep.
  • The mark roots are narrower than the full set. The epoch marks from READY snapshot manifest digests and gc_integrity_holds only. It does not mark from a workspace base or head, a checkpoint alias, an import session, an export job, a legal hold, or an administrative pin. Content those roots reference is protected by the safety grace timestamp when its age beats the cutoff.
  • The gc_deletion_plans.state value SKIPPED is unused. The schema permits it. The write path sets CANDIDATE then DELETED.

docs.title: systemd units
docs.text:
systemd units and the VM deployment procedure for AWC. This covers signed binaries, service units, a dedicated user and directories, capability boundaries, journald log integration, configuration, host enrollment, and drain, restart, and rollback behavior.

The artifacts are the systemd units and the packaging scripts:

  • the unit files: awcd.service, awc-worker.service, and awc-control.service;
  • the packaging scripts: build, sign, package, install, enroll, drain, and rollback. See Build and package.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Unit Role Privilege awcd.service per-host mount/cache daemon unprivileged awc user and minimal capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN for mount/cgroup/setns; /dev/fuse for FUSE) awc-worker.service background job-queue worker unprivileged awc user, no capabilities awc-control.service control plane REST and internal mTLS API unprivileged awc user

awcd is the only privileged service. It runs as the awc user but holds CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_SYS_ADMIN CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH CAP_CHOWN CAP_FOWNER (as ambient capabilities) so it can perform the privileged mount, OverlayFS, FUSE, and cgroup duties in its responsibilities. It also deliberately omits the mount-namespace-creating sandboxing directives so its FUSE and OverlayFS mounts stay visible in the host mount namespace. See the hardening section below and the in-unit comments for exactly what is and is not applied.

docs.title: Capability boundaries and hardening
docs.text:
The worker and control units take a maximal sandboxing posture: NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome, ProtectKernel*, ProtectControlGroups, ProtectClock, PrivateDevices, PrivateTmp, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_UNIX, and a SystemCallFilter=@system-service baseline.

awcd cannot take that posture. It is a privileged mount-publishing daemon whose FUSE base filesystem and per-workspace OverlayFS mounts must be visible in the host mount namespace — to clients, the worker, and the configure and acceptance checks. Each of ProtectSystem, ProtectHome, PrivateTmp, ProtectKernelModules, ProtectKernelLogs, ProtectClock, ProtectProc, and ReadWritePaths forces a private mount namespace whose mounts do not propagate back to the host (systemd.exec(5)). Using them hides awcd's own mounts from everything outside the unit. So awcd deliberately omits all eight — the same posture the Kubernetes DaemonSet takes to publish mounts (mountPropagation: Bidirectional).

What awcd keeps, and why each is safe:

  • ProtectHostname — UTS namespace only, not a mount namespace. It does not affect mount visibility.
  • StateDirectory, CacheDirectory, LogsDirectory, RuntimeDirectory, and ConfigurationDirectory — these bind-mount awcd's own directories but do not create a private mount namespace and do not disconnect mount propagation, so they do not hide awcd's mounts. RuntimeDirectory=awcd is also the sole creator of /run/awcd, the gRPC socket dir on the /run tmpfs, which the unprivileged awc user cannot create itself.
  • CapabilityBoundingSet and AmbientCapabilities=CAP_SYS_ADMIN CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH CAP_CHOWN CAP_FOWNER for mount, cgroup, and FUSE duties.
  • NoNewPrivileges, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, RestrictAddressFamilies, LockPersonality, RestrictRealtime, RestrictSUIDSGID, RemoveIPC, DevicePolicy=closed with DeviceAllow=/dev/fuse rw, and SystemCallFilter=@system-service @mount.

In short, awcd matches the worker and control posture on every axis that does not require a private mount namespace. The namespace-creating directives are the intentional, documented exception. systemd-analyze security awcd.service therefore reports a weaker score than a sandboxed unit, by design.

Validate offline with:

systemd-analyze verify   deploy/systemd/*.service
systemd-analyze security deploy/systemd/awcd.service   # hardening score

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: All three units log to journald (StandardOutput=journal, SyslogIdentifier=). Tail with journalctl -u awcd -f. Structured events flow through the same stderr stream. See observability.

docs.title: End-to-end VM procedure
docs.text:
# On a build host:
packaging/package.sh                     # -> dist/awc-<version>-<target>.tar.gz (signed)

# Copy the tarball to the VM, then as root:
tar xzf awc-<version>-<target>.tar.gz
cd awc-<target>
./install.sh                             # versioned /opt/awc layout, awc user, units, defaults
./enroll.sh --control-endpoint https://control.example.invalid
systemctl enable --now awcd awc-worker awc-control
journalctl -u awcd -f

For the full build and install steps, see Build and package and Install AWC.

docs.title: Host enrollment
docs.text: enroll.sh writes /etc/awc/awcd.toml and /etc/awc/awcd.env and creates the state directories. It is local enrollment: it mints a host id and writes a placeholder control endpoint. For a real deployment, replace the placeholder and provision mTLS identity. Host registration and the mTLS identity lifecycle are implemented, and awcd wires the control-plane client (lease lifecycle, checkpoint publisher, lease renewal) at startup. Outside AWC_DEV_MODE=1, awcd and awc-control MUST present TLS credentials or fail to start.

docs.title: Drain, restart, rollback
docs.text:
• Drain (drain.sh): sends SIGTERM to awcd, which reconciles live sessions against the authoritative lease, preserves uppers while the control plane is unreachable, and tears down mounts. systemctl stop bounds the drain via the unit's TimeoutStopSec. See Drain and restart a host.
  • Restart: Restart=on-failure with StartLimitBurst and StartLimitIntervalSec bounds flapping. Type=exec with an ExecStartPost liveness gate marks the unit active only once /healthz answers.
  • Rollback (rollback.sh): every install keeps its version under /opt/awc/versions/. current is a symlink. Rollback repoints the symlink, reloads systemd, and restarts the active services onto the older binaries. See Upgrade a deployment.

docs.title: Current scope (honest)
docs.text:
• awc-control.service serves the live control-plane API and requires its database, signing, service-token, and internal TLS configuration.
  • Featureless test builds can use a no-op base mount. Packaged releases enable the FUSE basefs. The unit grants /dev/fuse and the required mount capability.
  • Packaged workers include the S3 transport. Configure /etc/awc/worker.env with the deployment's durable CAS endpoint and credentials.

docs.title: gRPC API reference
docs.text:
AWC exposes two gRPC surfaces. Neither is the public HTTPS JSON API; for that, see REST API (v1).

Surface Package Served by Transport Caller HostService awc.host.v1 awcd Unix-domain socket awcctl, sandbox adapters LeaseService awc.control.v1 awc-control TCP, mTLS in production awcd CheckpointService awc.control.v1 awc-control TCP, mTLS in production awcd

The proto definitions are the authority for message shapes.

docs.title: Host API (Unix socket)
docs.text: Property Value Wire format gRPC over HTTP/2 Listen address Unix-domain socket Override Second positional argument to awcd, or the AWCD_SOCKET env var TLS None (file-system permissions gate the socket)

docs.title: Control-plane API (mTLS TCP)
docs.text:
Property Value Wire format gRPC over HTTP/2 Override AWC_CONTROL_GRPC_LISTEN Production TLS Mutual TLS (server + client cert) Dev plaintext Set AWC_DEV_MODE=1

mTLS environment variables, server side:

Variable Required unless dev Purpose AWC_CONTROL_TLS_CERT Yes Server certificate (PEM) AWC_CONTROL_TLS_KEY Yes Server private key (PEM) AWC_CONTROL_TLS_CLIENT_CA Yes CA that signs client certificates

mTLS environment variables, client side:

Variable Required for https:// Purpose AWC_CONTROL_TLS_CA Yes CA that signs the control-plane server cert AWC_CONTROL_TLS_CERT Yes Client certificate (PEM) AWC_CONTROL_TLS_KEY Yes Client private key (PEM) control_plane_endpoint Config Control-plane URI, for example https://control.example

Every control-plane handler binds the client certificate fingerprint to the registered host that owns the mount session. A request with no client certificate returns UNAUTHENTICATED, except in dev mode.

docs.title: HostService
docs.text:
Served by awcd on the Unix socket. Package awc.host.v1.

RPC Request Response MountWorkspace MountWorkspaceRequest MountWorkspaceResponse UnmountWorkspace UnmountWorkspaceRequest UnmountWorkspaceResponse CheckpointWorkspace CheckpointWorkspaceRequest stream CheckpointEvent GetHostStatus HostStatusRequest HostStatusResponse

docs.title: MountWorkspace
docs.text:
Mounts a workspace snapshot onto an authorized target. The host verifies the signed ticket without a synchronous control-plane call.

MountWorkspaceRequest

Field Type Required Notes signed_ticket string Yes Short-lived signed mount ticket target_path string Yes Must fall under an allow-listed root namespace_target string No Namespace bind target; empty means none mount_options map<string, string> No Read root_digest and labels here

MountWorkspaceResponse

Field Type Notes mount_session_id string New session id internal_merged_path string Per-session merged overlay view bound_target_path string Host path bound for the caller lease_generation uint64 Writer-lease fencing generation; 0 for read-only root_digest string Snapshot root digest the mount is pinned to cache_warmth_summary string Cache warmth summary

docs.title: UnmountWorkspace
docs.text:
Unmounts a previously mounted session.

UnmountWorkspaceRequest

Field Type Required Notes mount_session_id string Yes Session to unmount disposition MountDisposition No On-unmount disposition idempotency_key string No Deduplicates the unmount

UnmountWorkspaceResponse

Field Type Notes mount_session_id string Session that was unmounted checkpoint_result CheckpointResult Present only when disposition is CHECKPOINT

docs.title: CheckpointWorkspace
docs.text:
Server-streaming. Streams CheckpointProgress events, then one final CheckpointResult.

CheckpointWorkspaceRequest

Field Type Required Notes mount_session_id string Yes Session to checkpoint message string No Checkpoint message mode CheckpointMode No QUIESCED or COOPERATIVE idempotency_key string No Deduplicates the checkpoint labels map<string, string> No Provenance labels

CheckpointEvent is a oneof of progress or result.

Field Type Notes progress CheckpointProgress Progress update result CheckpointResult Final result; terminates the stream

CheckpointProgress

Field Type Notes stage string Current stage name completed_bytes uint64 Bytes processed so far total_bytes uint64 Total bytes expected

CheckpointResult

Field Type Notes snapshot_id string New snapshot id snapshot_digest string Snapshot digest workspace_version uint64 Workspace version after publish logical_bytes uint64 Logical bytes in the change set uploaded_unique_bytes uint64 New bytes uploaded to the CAS reused_object_bytes uint64 Bytes reused from the CAS changed_path_count uint64 Number of changed paths quiesce_duration_ms uint64 Quiesce duration in milliseconds

docs.title: GetHostStatus
docs.text:
Typed host lifecycle and mount state.

HostStatusRequest is empty.

HostStatusResponse

Field Type Notes state HostState Daemon lifecycle state base_mount_state BaseMountState Shared read-only base filesystem state base_mount_path string Path of the base filesystem mount active_mount_count uint32 Number of active mount sessions host_id string Registered host id version string Daemon version started_at_rfc3339 string Daemon start time, RFC 3339 UTC detail string Free-form detail, for example a degradation reason

docs.title: Host enums
docs.text:
MountDisposition

Value Meaning MOUNT_DISPOSITION_UNSPECIFIED Not set DISCARD_LOCAL Discard the upper layer CHECKPOINT Checkpoint before unmount PRESERVE_LOCAL Preserve the upper layer locally

CheckpointMode

Value Meaning CHECKPOINT_MODE_UNSPECIFIED Not set QUIESCED Freeze writes, then cut COOPERATIVE Best-effort, no freeze

HostState

Value Meaning HOST_STATE_UNSPECIFIED Not set STARTING Starting up HEALTHY Operating normally DEGRADED Operating with reduced function STOPPING Shutting down STOPPED Stopped

BaseMountState

Value Meaning BASE_MOUNT_STATE_UNSPECIFIED Not set NOT_MOUNTED Base filesystem not mounted MOUNTING Base filesystem mounting MOUNTED Base filesystem mounted UNMOUNTING Base filesystem unmounting FAILED Base filesystem failed to mount or unmount

docs.title: LeaseService
docs.text:
Served by awc-control over mTLS. Package awc.control.v1.

RPC Request Response ActivateWorkspaceLease ActivateWorkspaceLeaseRequest ActivateWorkspaceLeaseResponse RenewWorkspaceLease RenewWorkspaceLeaseRequest RenewWorkspaceLeaseResponse ReleaseWorkspaceLease ReleaseWorkspaceLeaseRequest ReleaseWorkspaceLeaseResponse

docs.title: ActivateWorkspaceLease
docs.text:
Confirms that the host completed the kernel mount and makes the writer lease publish-capable. An empty lease_id activates a read-only session.

ActivateWorkspaceLeaseRequest

Field Type Required Notes workspace_id string Yes ws_<ulid> lease_id string No Empty means read-only activation generation uint64 Yes Fencing generation mount_session_id string Yes Session being activated

ActivateWorkspaceLeaseResponse

Field Type Notes lease_state string ACTIVE for a writer; NONE for read-only mount_session_state string MOUNTED

docs.title: RenewWorkspaceLease
docs.text:
Renews or learns the fate of a writer lease. The control plane sets the new expiry from its own TTL, so a holder with a skewed clock still gets a coherent extension.

RenewWorkspaceLeaseRequest

Field Type Required Notes workspace_id string Yes ws_<ulid> lease_id string Yes lease_<ulid> generation uint64 Yes Fencing generation mount_session_id string No Optional session id

RenewWorkspaceLeaseResponse

Field Type Notes action RenewAction Verdict for this lease expires_at_rfc3339 string New expiry, RFC 3339 UTC, when action is EXTEND generation uint64 Generation known to the control plane detail string Free-form reason

RenewAction

Value Host action RENEW_ACTION_UNSPECIFIED Not set EXTEND Lease extended; the mount may continue writing REMOUNT_READ_ONLY Writer lease gone; remount read-only to keep serving REVOKE Mount revoked; unmount immediately WORKSPACE_GONE Workspace deleted or administratively locked

docs.title: ReleaseWorkspaceLease
docs.text:
Closes the authoritative mount session and releases its writer lease. An empty lease_id closes a read-only session.

ReleaseWorkspaceLeaseRequest

Field Type Required Notes workspace_id string Yes ws_<ulid> lease_id string No Empty means read-only release generation uint64 Yes Fencing generation mount_session_id string Yes Session being closed

ReleaseWorkspaceLeaseResponse

Field Type Notes lease_state string RELEASED for a writer; NONE for read-only mount_session_state string CLOSED

docs.title: CheckpointService
docs.text:
Served by awc-control over mTLS. Package awc.control.v1.

RPC Request Response PublishCheckpoint PublishCheckpointRequest PublishCheckpointResponse

docs.title: PublishCheckpoint
docs.text:
Atomically publishes a finished checkpoint as the new workspace head. The control plane completes every mutable update in one transaction. It validates expected_workspace_version, expected_prior_head_snapshot_id, and the lease fence inside that transaction.

PublishCheckpointRequest

Field Type Required Notes workspace_id string Yes ws_<ulid> expected_workspace_version uint64 Yes Optimistic-concurrency guard expected_prior_head_snapshot_id string Yes Head the publisher believes it replaces lease_id string Yes Lease under which the publish runs lease_generation uint64 Yes Lease fencing generation mount_session_id string No Session that produced the checkpoint snapshot_manifest_digest string Yes Content-addressed manifest digest idempotency_key string No Deduplicates the publish provenance CheckpointProvenance No Where the checkpoint came from statistics CheckpointStatistics No Byte and change accounting root_tree_digest string No New snapshot root tree digest; falls back to snapshot_manifest_digest if empty

PublishCheckpointResponse

Field Type Notes workspace_version uint64 Workspace version after publication head_snapshot_id string Snapshot id now recorded as head snapshot_manifest_digest string Manifest digest recorded published_at_rfc3339 string Publication time, RFC 3339 UTC

CheckpointProvenance

Field Type Notes parent_snapshot_id string Parent snapshot; falls back to expected_prior_head_snapshot_id message string Checkpoint message mode string QUIESCED or COOPERATIVE created_by string Principal; defaults to checkpoint if empty labels map<string, string> Provenance labels

CheckpointStatistics

Field Type Notes logical_bytes uint64 Logical bytes in the change set uploaded_unique_bytes uint64 New bytes uploaded reused_object_bytes uint64 Bytes reused from the CAS changed_path_count uint64 Changed path count quiesce_duration_ms uint64 Quiesce duration in milliseconds

docs.title: gRPC status codes
docs.text: Both surfaces return standard gRPC status codes. The control plane uses UNAUTHENTICATED, PERMISSION_DENIED, INVALID_ARGUMENT, NOT_FOUND, ABORTED, FAILED_PRECONDITION, and INTERNAL. The host API uses INVALID_ARGUMENT, NOT_FOUND, PERMISSION_DENIED, UNIMPLEMENTED, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, and FAILED_PRECONDITION.

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text:
The following behaviors are partial or absent in the current build:

  • MountWorkspace ignores namespace_target and returns UNIMPLEMENTED if the field is set.
  • MountWorkspace returns a fixed cache_warmth_summary of "cold"; it does not compute a real warmth summary.
  • UnmountWorkspace always returns checkpoint_result as None. The CHECKPOINT disposition is not honored as a combined unmount-plus-checkpoint operation.
  • CheckpointWorkspace returns UNIMPLEMENTED when no checkpoint runner is configured at daemon startup.
  • PublishCheckpoint records file_count as 0; CheckpointStatistics carries no file count, and the host client sets uploaded_unique_bytes, reused_object_bytes, and quiesce_duration_ms to 0.
  • The control-plane gRPC listener serves plaintext TCP when AWC_DEV_MODE=1 is set, with no client certificate check. Use dev mode only on a loopback or isolated network.

docs.title: REST API (v1) reference
docs.text:
The AWC control plane exposes a public HTTPS JSON API at /v1/*. This page lists every endpoint, its request and response fields, its auth and idempotency rules, and the error model. Where the shipped build lags the design, the page says so.

The host-local and internal gRPC methods (mount, unmount, checkpoint, lease renew, publish) are not REST. See gRPC services.

docs.title: Transport
docs.text: Property Value Wire format JSON (Content-Type: application/json) Transport HTTPS (spec §13.1) Base path /v1 Framework axum Body decoding serde_json; a malformed body returns INVALID_ARGUMENT Timestamps RFC 3339 UTC strings, for example 2026-08-05T15:00:00Z

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Every endpoint except GET /v1/health requires a bearer token (spec §13.2, §16.4).

Header Required Value Authorization Yes (except health) Bearer <token>

The control plane branches on the token shape (spec §13.2):

Principal kind Token form How it is verified USER OIDC id_token OIDC verifier (awc-auth) SERVICE_ACCOUNT awcsat1_<b64url(payload)>.<b64url(sig)> HMAC against the configured service-token key

A token that starts with awcsat1_ is parsed as a service-account token. Any other bearer token is treated as an OIDC id_token. If service-account tokens are not configured, an awcsat1_ token returns UNAUTHENTICATED.

Authorization is checked per request against the principal's project role (spec §16.4). A principal with no membership for the target project receives PERMISSION_DENIED. Cross-tenant access returns PERMISSION_DENIED without leaking existence (spec §16.5).

docs.title: Common headers
docs.text: Header Direction Purpose Spec Authorization Request Bearer credential (see above) §13.2 idempotency-key Request Deduplicates a mutation (mutations only) §13.1 x-request-id Both Tracing id; honored inbound, minted if absent, echoed outbound §13.1

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text:
All mutation endpoints accept the idempotency-key header (spec §13.1). A retry that carries the same key replays the committed result.

Property Value Replay window 24 hours (IDEMPOTENCY_TTL) Key scope tenant_id + principal + operation + key Conflict response IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (HTTP 409) Idempotent operations create import session, complete import, create workspace, fork workspace, issue mount ticket

POST :batchCheckObjects and all GET endpoints are reads. They do not read the idempotency-key header.

docs.title: Rate limiting
docs.text: Every authenticated request passes through a per-principal rate limiter keyed by tenant_id/subject (spec §16.10). When the bucket is empty the request returns RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (HTTP 429).

docs.title: Resource identifiers
docs.text:
Human-facing ids are opaque, prefix-qualified ULIDs of the form <prefix>_<ulid> (spec §9.1).

Type Prefix Appears in TenantId ten_ resource records ProjectId prj_ requests and records SnapshotId snap_ snapshots, workspaces WorkspaceId ws_ workspaces ImportSessionId import_ import sessions HostId host_ mount tickets LeaseId lease_ writer leases MountSessionId mount_ mount sessions

A mount ticket id uses tkt_. The opaque signed ticket string uses the awcmt1_ prefix (see Mount tickets).

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: The status column marks what the shipped build serves. "Implemented" means the route is served. "Specified" means a wire contract defines it but the router does not serve it.

docs.title: Import sessions
docs.text:
Method Path Status Spec POST /v1/import-sessions Implemented §13.3 POST /v1/import-sessions/{id}:batchCheckObjects Implemented §13.4 POST /v1/import-sessions/{id}:complete Implemented §13.5

The verb suffix travels in the same path segment, for example import_01J...:complete. The router captures the whole segment and splits on :. An unknown suffix returns NOT_FOUND.

docs.title: POST /v1/import-sessions
docs.text:
Opens a snapshot import session. Idempotent.

Request fields (CreateImportSessionRequest):

Field Type Required Notes project_id ProjectId Yes source_type enum Yes directory, git, tar, checkpoint normalization_policy enum Yes source-normalized, environment-preserving name string No labels map No Omitted when empty

Response (CreateImportSessionResponse):

Field Type Notes id ImportSessionId import_<ulid> state SnapshotState UPLOADING upload_endpoint string Opaque capability scoped to the tenant CAS prefix and session expires_at timestamp

The upload capability is limited to the tenant CAS prefix and the session (spec §13.3).

docs.title: POST /v1/import-sessions/{id}:batchCheckObjects
docs.text:
Checks which referenced objects are missing from the CAS. A read; not idempotency-keyed.

Request fields (BatchCheckObjectsRequest):

Field Type Required objects array of ObjectRef Yes

ObjectRef:

Field Type Notes digest Digest sha256:<hex> size_bytes u64 kind enum BLOB, FILE, TREE, SNAPSHOT

Response (BatchCheckObjectsResponse):

Field Type Notes missing array of Digest Digests absent from the CAS upload_urls map Optional. Digest string to presigned upload URL. Omitted when not offered

The service MAY return presigned upload URLs (spec §13.4). The shipped in-memory and database backends report missing only.

docs.title: POST /v1/import-sessions/{id}:complete
docs.text:
Completes the import and starts closure validation. Idempotent.

Request fields (CompleteImportRequest):

Field Type Required snapshot_manifest_digest Digest Yes declared_logical_bytes u64 Yes declared_file_count u64 Yes

Response (CompleteImportResponse):

Field Type Notes snapshot_id SnapshotId snap_<ulid> state SnapshotState VALIDATING

The snapshot becomes mountable only after closure validation sets it to READY (spec §13.5).

docs.title: Snapshots
docs.text: Method Path Status Spec GET /v1/snapshots Implemented §13 (list) GET /v1/snapshots/{id} Implemented §13 (get) GET /v1/snapshots/{left}:diff?right={right} Implemented (JSON only) §13.14

docs.title: GET /v1/snapshots
docs.text:
Lists snapshot metadata. The project_id query parameter is required.

Query parameters (ListSnapshotsRequest):

Parameter Type Required Notes project_id ProjectId Yes state SnapshotState No Client-side filter parent_snapshot_id SnapshotId No Children of this snapshot

Response (ListSnapshotsResponse):

Field Type snapshots array of Snapshot

The state and parent_snapshot_id filters are applied in the handler after the project listing, because the persistence port lists by project and tenant only.

docs.title: GET /v1/snapshots/{id}
docs.text:
Returns one snapshot record. An unknown id returns NOT_FOUND. A known id that belongs to another tenant returns PERMISSION_DENIED (the snapshot store fetches by id, then the handler enforces tenant match).

Snapshot resource:

Field Type Notes id SnapshotId tenant_id TenantId project_id ProjectId manifest_digest Digest Content identity of the snapshot manifest root_tree_digest Digest Root tree the manifest references state SnapshotState See Snapshot states logical_bytes u64 Logical, de-duplicated-summed size file_count u64 parent_snapshot_id SnapshotId Optional. None for an imported root source enum directory, git, tar, checkpoint normalization_policy enum source-normalized, environment-preserving created_by string created_at timestamp labels map Optional. Omitted when empty

docs.title: GET /v1/snapshots/{left}:diff
docs.text:
Compares two snapshot root trees and returns an inline change list. The right parameter is required.

Query parameters (DiffRequest):

Parameter Type Required Notes right SnapshotId Yes format enum No Default json

The shipped handler accepts format=json only. format=patch-bundle and format=tar return INVALID_ARGUMENT (spec §13.14).

Response (DiffResponse), tagged by kind:

kind Body Status result DiffResult Implemented (always returned) job DiffJob Specified for large diffs, not emitted

DiffResult:

Field Type Notes left SnapshotId right SnapshotId changes array of FileChange patch_bundle_digest Digest Optional. Set only for format=patch-bundle

FileChange:

Field Type Notes path string POSIX-style, relative to the snapshot root kind enum See Change kinds old_mode u32 Optional. Previous mode new_mode u32 Optional. New mode size_bytes u64 Optional. New content size content_digest Digest Optional. New content digest (file adds and modifies) unified_diff string Optional. Unified text diff

docs.title: Workspaces
docs.text:
Method Path Status Spec POST /v1/workspaces Implemented §13.6 GET /v1/workspaces/{id} Implemented §13.6 POST /v1/workspaces/{id}:fork Implemented §13.7 POST /v1/workspaces/{id}:issueMountTicket Implemented §13.8 POST /v1/workspaces/{id}:unmount Specified, not served §13.13 POST /v1/workspaces/{id}:acquireLease Specified, not served gRPC only POST /v1/workspaces/{id}:releaseLease Specified, not served gRPC only POST /v1/workspaces/{id}:revokeLease Specified, not served gRPC only

The router registers GET and POST on /v1/workspaces/{ws}. A GET with a verb suffix, or a POST verb other than fork and issueMountTicket, returns NOT_FOUND. The unmount and lease operations live on the gRPC services instead (see Current scope).

docs.title: POST /v1/workspaces
docs.text:
Creates a workspace from a READY snapshot. Idempotent. Requires the CreateWorkspace permission.

Request fields (CreateWorkspaceRequest):

Field Type Required Notes project_id ProjectId Yes snapshot_id SnapshotId Yes Must be READY and same-tenant name string No ttl_seconds u64 Yes Sets expires_at labels map No Omitted when empty

A non-READY source snapshot returns SNAPSHOT_NOT_READY.

docs.title: GET /v1/workspaces/{id}
docs.text:
Returns one workspace record. Requires ViewMetadata.

Workspace resource:

Field Type Notes id WorkspaceId tenant_id TenantId project_id ProjectId base_snapshot_id SnapshotId head_snapshot_id SnapshotId version u64 Optimistic-concurrency version state WorkspaceState See Workspace states writer_lease_generation u64 0 when no lease is held expires_at timestamp created_by string created_at timestamp labels map Optional. Omitted when empty

docs.title: POST /v1/workspaces/{id}:fork
docs.text:
Forks one or more workspaces from the base, head, or a specific retained snapshot. Idempotent. Requires ForkWorkspace.

Request fields (ForkWorkspaceRequest):

Field Type Required Notes from string Yes Wire key is from. Value is base, head, or a SnapshotId count u32 Yes Batch size ttl_seconds u64 Yes Sets expires_at for each child name_prefix string No

The API caps batch size at MAX_FORK_BATCH (1000). Larger fan-out uses repeated idempotent batches (spec §13.7).

Response (ForkWorkspaceResponse):

Field Type workspaces array of Workspace

docs.title: Mount tickets
docs.text: Method Path Status Spec POST /v1/workspaces/{id}:issueMountTicket Implemented §13.8

docs.title: POST /v1/workspaces/{id}:issueMountTicket
docs.text:
Mints a short-lived, signed mount ticket. Idempotent. For READ_WRITE the control plane acquires a single-writer lease and stamps its generation into the ticket. For READ_ONLY no lease is acquired. Permission maps to the mode: READ_WRITE needs MountWorkspace; READ_ONLY needs MountSnapshotReadOnly.

Request fields (IssueMountTicketRequest):

Field Type Required Notes host_id HostId Yes mode enum Yes READ_ONLY, READ_WRITE requested_ttl_seconds u64 No Default 300 seconds execution_cgroup string No For host-side accounting

An expired workspace (ttl_expires_at <= now) returns WORKSPACE_EXPIRED. A workspace that already holds a writer lease returns WRITER_LEASE_HELD.

Response (IssueMountTicketResponse):

Field Type Notes ticket MountTicket mount_session_id MountSessionId mount_<ulid> state MountSessionState AUTHORIZED

MountTicket:

Field Type Notes ticket_id string tkt_<ulid> tenant_id TenantId workspace_id WorkspaceId snapshot_id SnapshotId Head snapshot the mount is sealed against root_digest Digest Sealed root tree digest host_id HostId mode enum READ_ONLY, READ_WRITE lease_generation u64 Optional. Omitted for READ_ONLY target_policy TargetPolicy issued_at timestamp expires_at timestamp nonce string Single-use, defeats replay protocol_version u32 2 signed_ticket string awcmt1_<b64url(payload)>.<b64url(sig)>, Ed25519-signed

TargetPolicy:

Field Type Notes allowed_target_roots array of string The host refuses targets outside these roots

Defaults used by the control plane:

Constant Value DEFAULT_TICKET_TTL_SECONDS 300 DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS 90 TICKET_PROTOCOL_VERSION 2

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Method Path Status Auth GET /v1/health Implemented None

Returns the literal string ok. No bearer token required. Use it as a liveness probe.

docs.title: Snapshot states
docs.text:
SnapshotState serializes as SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (spec §12.1).

Value Mountable Readable UPLOADING No No VALIDATING No No READY Yes Yes FAILED No No DELETING No No DELETED No No DEGRADED No Yes

Only READY snapshots may be mounted or forked. DEGRADED snapshots are readable for reads that tolerate missing objects.

docs.title: Workspace states
docs.text:
WorkspaceState serializes as SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (spec §12.2).

Value CREATING FAILED IDLE MOUNTED CHECKPOINTING EXPIRING DELETED

docs.title: Mount session states
docs.text:
MountSessionState serializes as SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (spec §12.3).

Value REQUESTED AUTHORIZED PREPARING MOUNTED UNMOUNTING CLOSED FAILED

CLOSED and FAILED are terminal.

docs.title: Change kinds
docs.text:
ChangeKind serializes as kebab-case (spec §9.12).

Value Meaning add-file A new file was added modify-file An existing file changed delete-path A path was deleted create-directory A new directory was created delete-directory A directory was deleted change-mode Only the mode changed change-symlink A symlink was created or retargeted

docs.title: Diff formats
docs.text:
DiffFormat serializes as kebab-case (spec §13.14).

Value Status json Implemented (default) patch-bundle Specified, rejected by the handler tar Specified, rejected by the handler

docs.title: Error model
docs.text:
Errors use a stable, machine-readable code and include a request id (spec §13.1, §13.15). The top-level document is { "error": { ... } }.

ErrorBody:

Field Type Notes code ErrorCode Clients branch on this message string Human-readable; contains no secrets (spec §16.5) request_id string Optional. Omitted when absent retryable bool Whether bounded backoff may succeed

The HTTP status is advisory; the code is authoritative. The mapping below is what the shipped handler emits. For the full code reference, see Error codes.

Code HTTP Retryable UNAUTHENTICATED 401 No PERMISSION_DENIED 403 No HOST_NOT_AUTHORIZED 403 No NOT_FOUND 404 No INVALID_ARGUMENT 422 No OBJECT_MISSING 422 No OBJECT_CORRUPT 422 No MOUNT_UNSUPPORTED 422 No ALREADY_EXISTS 409 No IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT 409 No SNAPSHOT_NOT_READY 409 Yes WORKSPACE_BUSY 409 Yes STALE_LEASE_GENERATION 409 No WORKSPACE_VERSION_CONFLICT 409 No QUIESCE_FAILED 409 Yes WRITER_LEASE_HELD 409 Yes WORKSPACE_EXPIRED 410 No RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED 429 Yes LOCAL_IO_ERROR 500 Yes CHECKPOINT_PUBLICATION_FAILED 500 Yes OBJECT_STORE_UNAVAILABLE 503 Yes CONTROL_PLANE_UNAVAILABLE 503 Yes

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text: This section records where the shipped build differs from the spec.

docs.title: Implemented REST endpoints
docs.text:
The shipped router serves these routes:

  • POST /v1/import-sessions
  • POST /v1/import-sessions/{id}:batchCheckObjects
  • POST /v1/import-sessions/{id}:complete
  • GET /v1/snapshots
  • GET /v1/snapshots/{id}
  • GET /v1/snapshots/{left}:diff (JSON inline only)
  • POST /v1/workspaces
  • GET /v1/workspaces/{id}
  • POST /v1/workspaces/{id}:fork
  • POST /v1/workspaces/{id}:issueMountTicket
  • GET /v1/health

docs.title: Specified but not served as REST
docs.text:
The wire contracts for these operations exist, but the router does not register them as REST. The live transport is gRPC (see gRPC services):

  • POST /v1/workspaces/{id}:unmount (spec §13.13). The shipped path is the host-local gRPC method UnmountWorkspace.
  • POST /v1/workspaces/{id}:acquireLease, :releaseLease, :revokeLease. The spec does not define REST endpoints for these. A READ_WRITE mount acquires its writer lease implicitly through :issueMountTicket (spec §13.8). Lease activation, renewal, and release run over the control-plane gRPC LeaseService (ActivateWorkspaceLease, RenewWorkspaceLease, ReleaseWorkspaceLease). Spec §13.10 covers renewal, and §12.4 enumerates the lease states.

docs.title: Specified but not emitted
docs.text:
• Diff formats patch-bundle and tar (spec §13.14). The handler accepts format=json only and rejects the others with INVALID_ARGUMENT.
  • The deferred diff job (DiffResponse::Job, spec §13.14). The service always returns an inline DiffResponse::Result. The DiffJob contract exists but is not produced.
  • Batch-check presigned upload URLs (spec §13.4 "MAY"). The contract field upload_urls exists. The shipped backends report missing only and omit upload_urls.

docs.title: awc-control reference
docs.text:
awc-control is the control-plane API server (spec §8.1). It is a stateless service that runs behind a load balancer. It owns the external REST API and the trusted internal gRPC API. It MUST NOT proxy ordinary file reads or writes (spec §8.1).

The binary serves two listeners concurrently until shutdown:

  • the awc-api::v1 REST surface over HTTP (axum);
  • the internal awc-api::control gRPC surface over tonic.

docs.title: Listeners
docs.text:
Surface Env var Default Transport REST AWC_CONTROL_LISTEN 127.0.0.1:8080 HTTP (plaintext) gRPC AWC_CONTROL_GRPC_LISTEN 127.0.0.1:8081 mTLS outside dev; plaintext in dev

Both listeners bind before the server accepts traffic. The process blocks on a single ctrl-c or SIGTERM; both surfaces drain and exit together.

docs.title: Startup sequence
docs.text:
1. Read DATABASE_URL. Exit with an error if it is unset.
  2. Connect the Postgres pool (see Database pool).
  3. Apply pending migrations (see Migrations).
  4. Load the project membership graph from the project_memberships table.
  5. Load active token revocations from the token_revocations table.
  6. Build the object store from AWC_CAS_URL.
  7. Bind the REST and gRPC listeners and serve both until shutdown.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Default Meaning DATABASE_URL (none) Postgres connection string. Required. AWC_CONTROL_LISTEN 127.0.0.1:8080 REST listen address. AWC_CONTROL_GRPC_LISTEN 127.0.0.1:8081 gRPC listen address. AWC_DEV_MODE unset Set to 1 for local dev. Disables gRPC mTLS and relaxes the secret requirements below. AWC_SERVICE_TOKEN_KEY (none) HMAC key for service-account tokens. Required when AWC_DEV_MODE is not 1. AWC_MOUNT_TICKET_SEED (none) 64 hex chars (32 bytes). Signs mount tickets (spec §9.11). Required when AWC_DEV_MODE is not 1. AWC_MOUNT_TARGET_ROOTS /opt/sandboxes Comma-separated allow-list of mount target roots (spec §13.9). AWC_CAS_URL memory:// Object-store transport. One of memory:// or s3://. AWC_CONTROL_TLS_CERT (none) Server certificate path for gRPC mTLS. Required outside dev. AWC_CONTROL_TLS_KEY (none) Server private key path for gRPC mTLS. Required outside dev. AWC_CONTROL_TLS_CLIENT_CA (none) Trusted client CA path for gRPC mTLS. Required outside dev.

s3:// for AWC_CAS_URL selects the durable object store, but the s3 cargo feature is off in the default build (default = []). Rebuild with --features s3 to enable it; without the feature, an s3:// URL is rejected at startup.

docs.title: Local-dev bootstrap
docs.text:
These variables only take effect when AWC_DEV_BOOTSTRAP=1. They never apply to a production deployment.

Variable Default Meaning AWC_DEV_BOOTSTRAP unset Set to 1 to grant the dev principal the Admin role and mint a dev service token. AWC_DEV_TENANT ten_01arz3ndektsv4rrffq69g5fav Tenant for the bootstrap grant. AWC_DEV_PROJECT prj_01arz3ndektsv4rrffq69g5fav Project for the bootstrap grant. AWC_DEV_PRINCIPAL prin_01arz3ndektsv4rrffq69g5fav Principal that receives Admin.

When AWC_SERVICE_TOKEN_KEY is also set, the bootstrap logs a full-scope service token for the dev principal. The token is a dev-only credential with a fixed 24-hour lifetime.

docs.title: Database pool
docs.text:
The database layer builds a single Postgres connection pool and shares it across every repository. Each repository clones the pool; the pool is reference-counted.

Setting Value Override max_connections 16 None (fixed in code). min_connections sqlx default None. acquire_timeout sqlx default None.

The pool size is not exposed as an environment variable. It is fixed in code and requires a rebuild to change.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
Migrations are forward-only. The SQL migration files are embedded at compile time. There are no down or rollback files. The server applies pending migrations on startup before it accepts requests.

awc-control runs repos.migrate() after it connects. awc-worker also runs repos.migrate() on its own startup, so either binary can bring a fresh database up to the current schema.

The embedded set, in order:

Version file Adds 20260807000001_init.sql Core schema (see table below). 20260807000002_job_dedupe.sql jobs.dedupe_key. 20260807000003_gc_runs.sql gc_runs, gc_deletion_plans. 20260807000004_gc_integrity_holds.sql gc_integrity_holds. 20260808000005_project_memberships.sql project_memberships. 20260808000006_token_revocations.sql token_revocations.

The init migration creates these tables: tenants, projects, principals, hosts, snapshots, workspaces, workspace_leases, mount_sessions, mount_tickets, import_sessions, jobs, idempotency_keys, audit_events, retention_policies.

docs.title: REST surface
docs.text:
All /v1/* routes except /v1/health require a bearer token and pass through the per-principal rate limiter. Every mutation accepts an Idempotency-Key header (spec §13.1). Every response echoes an x-request-id header.

Method Path Spec Purpose POST /v1/import-sessions §13.3 Open an import session. POST /v1/import-sessions/:id:batchCheckObjects §13.4 Check which declared objects are missing. POST /v1/import-sessions/:id:complete §13.5 Complete an import; creates a VALIDATING snapshot. GET /v1/snapshots — List snapshot metadata. Requires project_id. No dedicated spec section. GET /v1/snapshots/:id — Get one snapshot's metadata. No dedicated spec section. GET /v1/snapshots/:id:diff §13.14 Compare two root trees. Only the inline json format is implemented. POST /v1/workspaces §13.6 Create a workspace from a READY snapshot. GET /v1/workspaces/:id — Get one workspace's metadata. No dedicated spec section (§13.6 defines the resource shape). POST /v1/workspaces/:id:fork §13.7 Fork one or more workspaces. POST /v1/workspaces/:id:issueMountTicket §13.8 Issue a signed mount ticket. GET /v1/health — Unauthenticated liveness probe. Returns ok.

Action verbs travel in the path segment after a colon (for example, /v1/import-sessions/import_01...:complete).

docs.title: gRPC surface
docs.text:
Both services are privileged internal RPCs. They are served with mutual TLS outside dev mode (spec §13.1). Each handler binds the client certificate fingerprint to the registered host that owns the mount session.

Service RPC Spec LeaseService ActivateWorkspaceLease — LeaseService RenewWorkspaceLease §13.10 LeaseService ReleaseWorkspaceLease — CheckpointService PublishCheckpoint §13.12

Only RenewWorkspaceLease (§13.10) and PublishCheckpoint (§13.12) have dedicated spec sections. ActivateWorkspaceLease and ReleaseWorkspaceLease are implemented in the control plane but not separately specified.

RenewWorkspaceLease is clock-independent. The control plane sets the new expiry from its own policy. The default renewal TTL is 90 seconds. A renewal returns one of: extend, remount read-only, revoke, or workspace gone.

PublishCheckpoint maps onto the control-plane checkpoint publish path. The control plane completes every mutable update for a checkpoint in a single PostgreSQL transaction (spec §13.12).

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The REST authenticator reads an Authorization: Bearer <token> header.

Credential Recognized by Verified with Service-account token awcsat1_ prefix AWC_SERVICE_TOKEN_KEY (HMAC). OIDC id token Any other bearer The configured OIDC verifier.

Project RBAC is loaded once at startup from the project_memberships table and held as an immutable serving snapshot. Restart the process to pick up durable membership changes.

docs.title: mTLS requirement
docs.text:
Outside dev mode, the gRPC listener requires mutual TLS. The mTLS setup configures a server identity and a required client CA, so a connection without a trusted client certificate never reaches a service handler.

AWC_DEV_MODE=1 disables mTLS. In dev mode the server serves plaintext gRPC and the handlers accept requests that carry no client certificate.

docs.title: Database failure (spec §17.6)
docs.text:
PostgreSQL MUST be deployed with automated failover and point-in-time recovery in production. The system MUST never reconstruct a mutable workspace head by guessing from object-store contents. Object-store snapshots are immutable candidates; PostgreSQL determines which one is the acknowledged head.

After a database restore, reconciliation compares published snapshot records, workspace versions, audit events, object-store snapshot manifests, and host-reported mount sessions. Unreferenced immutable objects stay safe and are reaped by garbage collection.

docs.title: Control-plane outage (spec §17.5)
docs.text:
Existing immutable reads and local writes do not require the control plane. During an outage:

  • a writer lease cannot be renewed authoritatively;
  • a checkpoint cannot be published;
  • a new mount ticket cannot be issued;
  • a workspace cannot be forked or deleted.

awcd MAY continue a writable mount through a bounded lease grace period. After grace expiration it MUST deny checkpoint publication and SHOULD remount the workspace read-only or pause the sandbox.

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text:
The following are specified but not yet implemented or exposed in the current build:

  • REST TLS. Spec §13.1 requires the external API to be HTTPS. The binary serves REST as plaintext HTTP and expects TLS termination upstream (for example, at a load balancer). There is no in-process REST TLS option.
  • Rate limiting. Spec §16.10 describes admission throttling. The server constructs an unlimited limiter. There is no environment variable to set a limit.
  • OIDC discovery. The server wires a static OIDC verifier with an empty trusted set. Real OIDC discovery is a follow-up. Until then, only service-account tokens authenticate, and only when AWC_SERVICE_TOKEN_KEY is set.
  • gRPC request id. PublishCheckpoint does not yet surface an x-request-id from gRPC metadata into the audit record.
  • Durable membership seeding. The in-memory membership store loads only from project_memberships at startup. There is no admin API to mutate it at runtime.

docs.title: awc-worker reference
docs.text:
awc-worker is a background process. It drains the PostgreSQL job queue and dispatches each claimed job by kind to a handler (spec §8.2). The worker only claims and runs jobs. It does not enqueue them. The control plane enqueues jobs.

The process runs a bounded pool of workers. Each worker loops: claim a ready job, run the handler, record the outcome, then claim the next job.

docs.title: Startup
docs.text:
The startup sequence is fixed:

  1. Read DATABASE_URL and AWC_CAS_URL. Both are required.
  2. Connect the database pool.
  3. Apply pending migrations (Repositories::migrate).
  4. Select the object store from the AWC_CAS_URL scheme.
  5. Register the job handlers.
  6. Start the supervisor pool.

If any step fails, the process prints awc-worker: <error> to standard error and exits 1. Startup error messages carry no secrets (spec §16.5). Database errors surface by type and message, never by the connection string.

docs.title: Migrate on startup
docs.text: The worker runs schema migrations before it accepts jobs. The call is Repositories::migrate, which runs the sqlx MIGRATOR against the pool. Point two workers at one database and both migrate; sqlx tracks the applied set in the migration bookkeeping table.

docs.title: Object store selection
docs.text:
The AWC_CAS_URL scheme selects the content-addressed object store. The same store backs snapshot validation, the integrity scrub, and durable garbage collection.

Scheme Store Requirement memory:// In-process store Local and integration use. s3:// S3-compatible transport Requires the s3 cargo feature. Configure it with the AWC_S3_* variables (spec §16.3). any other none Startup error.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 The supervisor ran and shut down cleanly. 1 A startup or runtime error occurred.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Default Purpose DATABASE_URL required PostgreSQL connection string for the job queue. AWC_CAS_URL required Object-store URL. Selects the transport by scheme. AWC_WORKER_ID awc-worker Per-process id. Each concurrent worker appends -<n> to its leases. AWC_WORKER_CONCURRENCY 4 Bounded worker count. The pool spawns this many tasks. AWC_WORKER_LEASE_SECS 300 Visibility-lease length, in seconds. AWC_WORKER_POLL_INTERVAL_MS 1000 Idle poll interval, in milliseconds. The worker sleeps this long when no job is ready. AWC_RETENTION_GRACE_SECS 86400 How long an EXPIRING workspace stays reversible before it may be reaped (spec §12.5). Used by workspace_expire. AWC_GC_GRACE_SECS 86400 Durable-GC safety grace, in seconds. Objects newer than now - grace are never swept (spec §18.4). Used by gc_sweep. AWC_GC_BATCH_SIZE 1000 Maximum candidates deleted per GC epoch. Used by gc_sweep. AWC_GC_CANARY_SIZE 10 Size of the leading canary batch per GC epoch. Used by gc_sweep. AWC_GC_DRY_RUN false Plan only; delete nothing (spec §18.3). Accepted true values: 1, true, TRUE.

Integer variables that fail to parse cause a startup error. The error names the setting and the parse failure.

docs.title: Job kinds
docs.text:
The worker registers one handler per kind. An unknown kind is a permanent failure. The supervisor dead-letters it; it does not retry.

Kind Handler Payload key Work snapshot_validate ValidationHandler snapshot_id Verifies the content-addressed closure of a VALIDATING snapshot. Moves it to READY, FAILED, or skips it if already terminal. snapshot_scrub ScrubHandler snapshot_id Re-verifies every object in a READY snapshot's closure. Marks decayed snapshots DEGRADED and pins their closure against GC. Emits the snapshot.scrub audit event. workspace_expire WorkspaceExpireHandler workspace_id Advances one workspace through the TTL state machine (spec §12.5). snapshot_retain SnapshotRetainHandler snapshot_id Evaluates retention for one snapshot. gc_sweep GcHandler tenant_id Runs one durable-GC epoch for a tenant (spec §18.3).

A malformed payload is a permanent failure for every kind. The job is dead-lettered; it is not retried.

docs.title: Job lifecycle
docs.text: A job moves through these states: PENDING, RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED.

docs.title: Claim and lease
docs.text: Each worker calls claim with its per-worker id and the lease length. A claim sets the job to RUNNING and records locked_by and locked_until. The claim commits before the handler runs, so handler I/O stays outside the database transaction (spec §8.2).

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
A handler returns one of three outcomes. The supervisor records it.

Outcome Record action Final state Complete(result) complete COMPLETED Retry(error) fail with backoff PENDING, or FAILED once attempts reaches max_attempts Fail(error) dead_letter FAILED

A job whose subject failed is still a completed job. For example, a snapshot that does not close produces a COMPLETED validation job with the verdict in result.

docs.title: Retry and dead-letter
docs.text:
Retry is for transient store errors. The supervisor reschedules the job with a bounded exponential backoff and full jitter (spec §17.7, §8.2). The retry path dead-letters the job once attempts reaches max_attempts.

max_attempts is a per-job column. The producer sets it at enqueue time; the worker reads it from the row. The worker does not set max_attempts.

Fail is permanent. It dead-letters immediately. The worker never retries a Fail.

docs.title: Backoff
docs.text:
The deterministic base is 5 * 2^attempts seconds, capped at 300 seconds.

Attempts (after this claim) Base delay 0 5 s 1 10 s 2 20 s 3 40 s >= 6 300 s (cap)

Full jitter adds a uniform [0, base] offset. A retried job's total delay lies in [base, 2 * base]. Each worker seeds one xorshift32 PRNG from its worker id, so retried jobs across the pool do not fire on the same tick.

docs.title: Cancellation and lease expiry
docs.text:
After the handler runs, the supervisor re-reads the job. If the job is no longer RUNNING under this worker, the supervisor discards its outcome. This covers two cases:

  • The job was cancelled while the handler ran.
  • The lease expired and another worker reclaimed the job.

Validation is idempotent, so a concurrent run is harmless (spec §8.2).

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The worker registers three instruments when the supervisor runs with observability attached (spec §19.2). Label values are closed-set.

Metric Type Labels When recorded awc_background_jobs_total counter kind, outcome Once per processed job. awc_background_job_lag_seconds gauge kind Once per processed job. The ready-to-processed lag, in seconds. awc_api_errors_total counter component=worker On a transient store error during the claim or record step.

The outcome label is a closed set.

outcome value Job state that produced it completed COMPLETED failed FAILED cancelled CANCELLED retried PENDING (rescheduled) other any unrecognised state

The metrics registry caps distinct label-sets per instrument at 128. Recordings beyond the cap roll into the synthetic cardinality_overflow label value.

docs.title: Structured events
docs.text:
The worker emits one structured event per processed job to standard error (spec §19.5). The event id is job_<job-id>. It carries these fields: kind, outcome, state, attempts. Events carry no secrets (spec §16.5): only the kind and an outcome class, never a payload or error text.

Outcome Log level Message completed info job completed retried warn job retried after transient failure failed error job dead-lettered cancelled error job cancelled

docs.title: Signals
docs.text: SIGINT and SIGTERM trigger a graceful shutdown. A shared stop signal is sent to every worker. Each worker stops accepting new claims and exits after the job it is mid-flight on. The supervisor returns once all workers have joined.

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text:
The MVP spec (§8.2) lists more job types than the current build implements. The worker ships handlers for these kinds only: snapshot_validate, snapshot_scrub, workspace_expire, snapshot_retain, and gc_sweep.

Spec §8.2 job types with no shipped handler:

  • Git import
  • Snapshot logical-size calculation
  • Structural diff generation for large diffs
  • CAS garbage-collection planning (the shipped gc_sweep runs the epoch; the separate planning job is not implemented)
  • Object-store inventory ingestion
  • Billing aggregation
  • Host-health reconciliation
  • Audit export

The worker does not enqueue jobs and does not expose a control API. Job scheduling is the responsibility of the control plane.

No trusted recovery store is wired today. The scrub handler detects decay and degrades without attempting replica recovery (the recovery source is None).

docs.title: awcctl command reference
docs.text: awcctl is the reference CLI for AWC (spec §5.1, §8.9). It creates snapshots, forks and mounts workspaces, checkpoints, diffs, and exports. Every mutation honors an idempotency key (spec §13.1).

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
awcctl [GLOBAL FLAGS] <command> [FLAGS] [POSITIONAL]

Global flags are declared global, so you may place them before or after the subcommand. None of the global flags has a short form.

docs.title: Transports
docs.text:
awcctl speaks two transports (spec §8.9).

Transport Endpoint Used for Host daemon (awcd) Unix socket, gRPC awc.host.v1 status, workspace mount, workspace checkpoint, workspace unmount Control plane (awc-control) HTTPS, JSON awc-api::v1 snapshot *, workspace fork, workspace status, mount ticket in workspace mount

workspace mount uses both transports. It issues a signed ticket over the control plane, then redeems the ticket at the host daemon (spec §13.8, §13.9).

docs.title: Global flags
docs.text:
Flag Env var Type Default Effect --output AWC_OUTPUT enum text Output format. Values: text, json. --quiet AWC_QUIET bool false Suppress progress output on stderr. Results still print. --host-socket AWC_HOST_SOCKET path /run/awcd/awcd.sock Path to the local awcd Unix socket. --control-endpoint AWC_CONTROL_ENDPOINT URL none Base URL of the control plane, for example https://control.example. --token AWC_TOKEN string none Bearer token for control-plane auth. The env value is hidden from help. --tenant AWC_TENANT string none Tenant id. Required for snapshot upload. --project AWC_PROJECT string none Project id. Required for most control-plane commands. --idempotency-key AWC_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY string none Idempotency key for the next mutating request (spec §13.1).

--version and -V print the CLI version. --help and -h print help. Both are available on every subcommand.

Under --output json, results are printed as JSON on stdout and progress on stderr. Errors are printed as a JSON document on stdout plus a human-readable line on stderr. The JSON error document carries the control-plane error code, the message, the exit code, and the request id.

Retries

Control-plane requests retry transient failures with bounded exponential backoff and full jitter (spec §17.5). Defaults: 3 attempts, 200 ms base, 5 s cap. Retryable HTTP statuses are 408, 425, 429, and 5xx except 501 and 505. Mutations are safe to retry because of the idempotency key.

docs.title: Top-level commands
docs.text: Command Summary status Show host-daemon health and mount state. snapshot Create, inspect, list, diff, and export snapshots. workspace Fork, inspect, mount, checkpoint, and unmount workspaces.

docs.title: awcctl status
docs.text:
Shows host lifecycle and base-mount state from the host daemon. The GetHostStatus RPC has no dedicated spec section (do not confuse it with §13.9, which is MountWorkspace). Uses the host transport only.

awcctl status

Text-mode fields: host, state, version, basefs, basefs path, mounts, started, and detail when non-empty.

docs.title: snapshot create
docs.text:
Creates an immutable snapshot from a prepared directory through a resumable upload (spec §5.2, §13.3 to §13.5). Uses the control transport and an object store.

awcctl snapshot create --from-dir <DIR> [--name <NAME>] [FLAGS]
Flag Type Required Default Effect --from-dir path yes Source directory to import. --name string no none Human-friendly snapshot name. --source-type enum no directory Source kind. Values: directory, git, tar. --normalization enum no source-normalized Metadata normalization policy. Values: source-normalized, environment-preserving. --object-store-endpoint URL no none Object store for resumable upload. The scheme selects the backend, for example s3://my-bucket or memory://. --label KEY=VALUE no none Label. Repeat the flag to add more than one. --idempotency-key string no none Overrides the global key for this upload.

The object store is selected from --object-store-endpoint, else the AWC_CAS_URL env var. The value scheme selects the backend: memory:// for the in-memory store, s3:// for S3-compatible storage. The s3:// scheme requires the s3 build feature. S3 credentials come from the AWC_S3_* env vars.

Text-mode fields: snapshot_id, state, manifest, logical_bytes, file_count.

docs.title: snapshot inspect
docs.text:
Shows one snapshot's metadata. Uses the control transport. (The spec gives no dedicated read section; §13.5 is the import-completion RPC.)

awcctl snapshot inspect <ID>
Argument Type Required Effect ID snapshot id yes Snapshot id to inspect.

Text-mode fields: id, state, manifest, root tree, files, bytes, source, normalized, and parent when set.

docs.title: snapshot list
docs.text:
Lists snapshots, with optional filters. Uses the control transport. (The spec gives no dedicated list section; §13.5 is the import-completion RPC.)

awcctl snapshot list [--project <ID>] [--state <STATE>] [--parent <ID>]
Flag Type Required Default Effect --project project id no none Filter by project. --state string no none Filter by snapshot state. --parent snapshot id no none Filter by parent snapshot.

docs.title: snapshot diff
docs.text:
Compares two snapshots (spec §13.14). Uses the control transport.

awcctl snapshot diff <LEFT> <RIGHT> [--format <FORMAT>]
Argument Flag Type Required Default Effect LEFT snapshot id yes Left snapshot id. RIGHT snapshot id yes Right snapshot id. --format enum no json Output format. Values: json, patch-bundle, tar.

For json, a structured result prints on stdout. For patch-bundle and tar, the raw artifact streams to stdout. For large diffs, the control plane may return a job id instead of an inline result.

docs.title: snapshot export
docs.text:
Exports the changes of one snapshot against another (spec §13.14). Uses the control transport.

awcctl snapshot export <SNAPSHOT> --against <BASE> [--format <FORMAT>] [--out <PATH>]
Argument Flag Type Required Default Effect SNAPSHOT snapshot id yes Snapshot whose changes are exported. --against snapshot id yes Base snapshot to compare against. --format enum no patch-bundle Output format. Values: json, patch-bundle, tar. --out path no - Output file. Use - for stdout.

Spec and code disagree

Spec §5.1 names the output flag --output. The code implements --out. This page documents the code, which is what ships.

docs.title: workspace fork
docs.text:
Forks private workspaces (spec §5.3, §13.6, §13.7). Uses the control transport. There are two modes:

  • --snapshot forks one workspace from a snapshot (POST /v1/workspaces).
  • --workspace batch-forks from an existing workspace (POST /v1/workspaces/{id}:fork).

You must pass exactly one of --snapshot or --workspace.

awcctl workspace fork --snapshot <ID> --ttl <DURATION> [FLAGS]
awcctl workspace fork --workspace <ID> --ttl <DURATION> [--from <SRC>] [--count <N>] [FLAGS]
Flag Type Required Default Effect --snapshot snapshot id one of none Fork one workspace from this snapshot. --workspace workspace id one of none Batch-fork from this existing workspace. --from enum or id no head With --workspace. Values: base, head, or a snapshot id. --count integer no 1 Number of workspaces. Only with --workspace. --ttl duration yes Workspace lifetime, for example 2h. --name string no none Name for one fork, or name prefix for a batch. --label KEY=VALUE no none Label. Repeat the flag to add more than one.

With --snapshot, --count must be 1. The --snapshot path requires --project.

A --ttl value is a number with an optional unit. Units: s, sec, secs, seconds; m, min, mins, minutes; h, hr, hrs, hours; d, day, days. A bare number is seconds.

docs.title: workspace status
docs.text:
Shows one workspace's metadata. Uses the control transport. (The spec gives no dedicated read section; §13.6 is the create-workspace RPC.)

awcctl workspace status <ID>
Argument Type Required Effect ID workspace id yes Workspace id to inspect.

Text-mode fields: id, state, base, head, version, lease gen, expires.

docs.title: workspace mount
docs.text:
Mounts a workspace onto an authorized target (spec §5.4, §13.8, §13.9). Uses both transports.

awcctl workspace mount <WORKSPACE> --target <PATH> [--read-only]
Argument Flag Type Required Default Effect WORKSPACE workspace id yes Workspace id to mount. --target path yes Target mount path. Must fall under the host allow-list. --read-only bool no false Mount read-only. Default is read-write.

Text-mode fields: session, target, merged, root, lease gen.

Spec and code disagree

Spec §5.1 shows --mode read-write and --mode read-only. The code implements a single --read-only boolean flag. This page documents the code.

docs.title: workspace checkpoint
docs.text:
Persists an immutable checkpoint of a mounted workspace (spec §5.5, §13.11). Uses the host transport. The positional argument is the mount session id that workspace mount returned.

awcctl workspace checkpoint <MOUNT_SESSION_ID> [--message <MSG>] [--mode <MODE>] [FLAGS]
Argument Flag Type Required Default Effect MOUNT_SESSION_ID string yes Mount session id from mount. --message string no none Checkpoint message. --mode enum no quiesced Checkpoint mode. Values: quiesced, cooperative. --label KEY=VALUE no none Label. Repeat the flag to add more than one. --idempotency-key string no none Overrides the global key for this checkpoint.

Progress streams to stderr as checkpoint <stage>: <done>/<total> bytes.

Text-mode fields: snapshot, digest, version, logical bytes, uploaded bytes, changed paths.

Spec and code disagree

Spec §5.1 passes a workspace id to checkpoint. The code takes the mount session id. This page documents the code.

docs.title: workspace unmount
docs.text:
Unmounts a session with a chosen disposition for local changes (spec §11.11, §13.13). Uses the host transport.

awcctl workspace unmount <MOUNT_SESSION_ID> [--disposition <DISP>] [--idempotency-key <KEY>]
Argument Flag Type Required Default Effect MOUNT_SESSION_ID string yes Mount session id. --disposition enum no discard-local Disposition for local changes. Values: discard-local, checkpoint, preserve-local. --idempotency-key string no none Overrides the global key for this unmount.

docs.title: Argument value enums
docs.text: Enum Values --output text, json --source-type directory, git, tar --normalization source-normalized, environment-preserving --from (workspace fork) base, head, or any snapshot id --mode (checkpoint) quiesced, cooperative --disposition (unmount) discard-local, checkpoint, preserve-local --format (diff, export) json, patch-bundle, tar

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Every failure maps to a stable exit code (spec Appendix E). The exit code is the authoritative contract for CI and sandbox integrations.

Code Meaning Example cause 0 Success Command completed. 2 Invalid command or argument Unknown subcommand, bad id, missing required flag, clap parse error, INVALID_ARGUMENT, MOUNT_UNSUPPORTED. 3 Authentication or authorization failure UNAUTHENTICATED, PERMISSION_DENIED, HOST_NOT_AUTHORIZED. 4 Resource not found NOT_FOUND. 5 Conflict, busy workspace, or stale version ALREADY_EXISTS, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, SNAPSHOT_NOT_READY, WORKSPACE_EXPIRED, WORKSPACE_BUSY, STALE_LEASE_GENERATION, WORKSPACE_VERSION_CONFLICT, WRITER_LEASE_HELD. 6 Local host or mount failure Host socket unreachable, local I/O error, gRPC UNIMPLEMENTED. 7 Object-store or remote I/O failure OBJECT_MISSING, OBJECT_STORE_UNAVAILABLE, transport error, decode error. 8 Checkpoint or integrity failure OBJECT_CORRUPT, CHECKPOINT_PUBLICATION_FAILED, QUIESCE_FAILED, checkpoint stream ended with no result. 9 Resource limit exceeded RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. 10 Temporary control-plane unavailability CONTROL_PLANE_UNAVAILABLE, gRPC UNAVAILABLE.

For the full list of error codes and their retryability, see error codes. Under --output json, machine consumers SHOULD parse the JSON error document instead of relying on the numeric code alone (spec Appendix E).

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text:
This page reflects the current build of awcctl.

  • The CLI implements the subcommands and flags listed above. There is no workspace delete, workspace lease, or snapshot delete subcommand in the current build, even where the spec discusses related lifecycle behavior.
  • Git and tar source import (--source-type git, --source-type tar) are declared by the CLI and accepted by the parser. The launch-critical path is local-directory import (spec §5.2).
  • The --label flag is a key-value pair. The CLI rejects an empty key or a value without an = sign.
  • Lease renewal, checkpoint publication, and object-store batch checks are internal control-plane or host-daemon operations. They are not exposed as awcctl subcommands.
  • The mount --mode flag shown in spec §5.1 is not implemented. Use --read-only.
  • The export --output flag shown in spec §5.1 is not implemented. Use --out.

docs.title: awcd daemon reference
docs.text: awcd is the privileged per-host daemon. One instance runs on each compute host. It maintains the shared read-only snapshot filesystem, the host-local content cache, private upper directories, and OverlayFS and bind mounts. It serves its host API on a Unix-domain socket (spec §8.3).

docs.title: Invocation
docs.text:
awcd <config.toml|-> [socket-path]
Argument Required Description config.toml yes Path to a TOML config file. Pass - to load environment only. socket-path no Path for the Unix-domain gRPC socket.

The socket path resolves in this order:

  1. The second positional argument.
  2. The AWCD_SOCKET environment variable.
  3. /run/awcd/awcd.sock.

docs.title: Configuration sources
docs.text:
awcd loads configuration in layers. Later layers override earlier ones.

file < environment (AWC_*) < flags
Source How it is read Config file First positional argument. Parsed as TOML. Environment Variables prefixed with AWC. Nested keys use __. Flags Not exposed on the awcd command line in this build.

The packaged systemd unit reads /etc/awc/awcd.toml and imports /etc/awc/awcd.env through EnvironmentFile.

docs.title: Config keys
docs.text:
Key Environment variable Default Notes host_id AWC_HOST_ID required Must parse as a host_<ulid>. control_plane_endpoint AWC_CONTROL_PLANE_ENDPOINT required http or https. https is required outside dev mode. basefs_mount AWC_BASEFS_MOUNT required Absolute path.
